general insurance - private insurance

Property Insurance

In the Kingdom of Cambodia, the fast-growing real estate sector has significantly enhanced the value of assets, underscoring the necessity for comprehensive protection against unforeseen incidents. Property insurance offers a safeguard for your buildings, covering a wide array of accidental damages including those caused by Fire, Water Damage, Floods, Explosions, Windstorms, Landslides, and Vehicle Impacts among others.

Get a Free quote

item.title: About AG Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
About AG Insurance Broker

Your Trusted Insurance Broker Since 2006

Founded in 2006, AG Insurance Broker has been at the forefront of the Cambodian insurance market, offering a wide range of insurance products and expert consultancy services tailored to the unique needs of individuals and businesses across the Kingdom. With over 20 years of experience, we’ve built a reputation for integrity, reliability, and customer-centric service. Our team of dedicated professionals works closely with leading international and local insurers, ensuring our clients receive the best protection and the most competitive rates.

Linkedin Envelope

Our Mission

Our mission is simple:
to safeguard what matters most to our clients.

Whether you're looking for personal health insurance or comprehensive business insurance solutions, our commitment is to provide you with unparalleled support and guidance throughout the entire process, from selecting the right coverage to making a claim.

Meet our team of professionals

Download our Company Profile

Our 20th Anniversary celebration

Relive the celebration

A Legacy of Trust

Since our inception, we have successfully helped thousands of individuals, families, and businesses secure the insurance coverage they need, protecting their financial future and providing peace of mind. We are proud of our longstanding relationships with both our clients and partners, as well as our continued role in supporting Cambodia’s growing insurance market.

Our Commitment to Cambodia

As a homegrown Cambodian company, AG Insurance Broker is committed to contributing to the social and economic development of the country. We believe in giving back to the community through various initiatives, including supporting education, local healthcare initiatives, and providing insurance awareness programs to underserved areas. We are proud to be a trusted partner in Cambodia’s progress, offering financial protection to empower both individuals and businesses.

Why Choose AG Cambodia?

Extensive Network of Insurers

We work with a broad range of reputable insurers, giving you access to a variety of coverage options.

Tailored Insurance Solutions

No two clients are alike. We take the time to understand your needs and craft personalized solutions that fit your lifestyle or business requirements.

Exceptional Customer Service

Our clients are at the heart of everything we do. With AG Cambodia, you're never just a policy number. We're here to support you, offering prompt and knowledgeable service at every stage of your journey.

Expertise Across Sectors

Whether you're an individual seeking international health insurance, a business owner needing property and casualty insurance, or a corporate client requiring tailored risk management solutions, we’ve got you covered.

Follow us on 

Innovative Technology

Our team continuously adopts modern technologies to streamline processes, ensuring a seamless experience for our clients, from easy-to-understand policy options to efficient claims handling.

item.title: Health Insurance in Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
International Health Insurance for Expats

International service, local presence

The instant quotation form will give you a very good estimate in record time. We base this estimate from three of our best plans from these three brands: Luma, ACS and April.

INSTANT QUOTATION

Get a quick estimate within minutes. Fill out this short form, and check your email. This form is for lone individuals, if you want a tailored quotation for your family click here

Please enable JavaScript in your browser to complete this form.
Date of Birth *

Health is likely to be at the top of your priority list

Health is likely to be at the top of your priority list, especially when living in a south east Asian sub-tropical country such as Cambodia. Moreover, the current medical and sanitation environment, though having made huge progress in the past decade, is still lacking facilities and expertise. Thus implying that in case of severe emergency, Bangkok remains the closest facility.

Health Insurance is your first insurance need whether for your family or for your corporate expatriate team. Healthcare costs can reach very high amounts and selecting the right plan that will respond to your needs can be quite an exercise: insurance companies do not provide the same coverage, they also don’t all have the same protocols, criteria and administrative process and premiums differ from a provider to another. Choosing the right plan is not easy and this is where AG Cambodia is her to help.

Non-resident health insurance

You and your family moved to Cambodia and you are looking to offer them a reliable international health coverage, then visit the next page Click Here

Tourist health insurance

You are traveling outside of your country of residence, whether for business or leisure, we have some great packages for short term insurance Click Here

Employee's health insurance

You are employing staff, whether for your business or your household, AG Cambodia can help you get them properly covered at all time Click Here

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Health Insurance Cambodia; from long term to holiday coverage
Health insurance Cambodia should be on the top of your list of priorities if you just moved into Cambodia. Rest assured, we have served many before you.

health insurance - private insurance

Travel Insurance

A short business trip or a family holiday can turn into an expensive problem without the right cover in place. Travel insurance protects against emergency medical care and evacuation abroad, trip cancellation and interruption, and baggage delay or loss, for single trips or on an annual multi-trip basis.

It's available for individuals, families, or teams travelling for business, and can be arranged alongside your other AG Cambodia policies for a single point of contact if anything happens while you're away.

item.title: General Insurance in Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
General Insurance

in Cambodia

At AG Cambodia, we help individuals, families, and businesses protect what matters most. As a licensed insurance broker based in Phnom Penh, our role is to guide clients through the wide range of insurance solutions available in Cambodia and identify the coverage that best fits their needs.

Unlike an insurance company that promotes its own products, a broker works on behalf of the client. We compare policies from some of the most reliable insurers operating in Cambodia in order to find the most appropriate protection at a competitive price. Our team also supports you throughout the life of your policy — from the initial quotation to policy management and claims assistance when needed. Insurance needs vary widely depending on your situation, whether you are an individual seeking protection for your vehicle or home, or a business looking to manage operational risks. Our general insurance services in Cambodia cover a broad range of areas designed to protect both personal and professional assets.

item.title: Long term health Insurance for expats
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
health insurance - private insurance

International health insurance

Living in Cambodia is generally straightforward, until you need medical treatment. Quality private healthcare is available, but serious treatment can quickly become expensive, good medical care here comes at international prices, and the right hospital network can be the difference between a manageable bill and a financial shock. In some situations, you may also need to travel elsewhere in Southeast Asia for specialist care.

That is why the right health insurance is about more than simply paying hospital bills. It is about knowing where you can be treated, what your insurer will actually cover, and what happens if the care you need isn't available locally — and having a broker on the ground who knows the answers.

Get a Free quote

For 20 years, AG Insurance Broker has helped expatriates, individuals and families in Cambodia answer exactly those questions. We know the local hospital network, the doctors and the care pathways in detail, and we work only with established international insurers selected among the leaders in their market, solid, reliable and responsive solutions, backed by a local team on hand to facilitate pre-authorisations and reimbursements. All our solutions guarantee renewal, whatever your claims history.

Our plans give you access to trusted local and regional hospital networks, structured across local, regional (Southeast Asia) and worldwide cover, including medical evacuation. Plans can include dependants and family cover and maternity options, with a claims process built around direct billing; so the clinics you actually use are paid directly by the insurer, rather than leaving you to fund treatment and reclaim it later.

Depending on the plan you choose, your cover can include treatment in Cambodia, throughout Southeast Asia or worldwide, together with medical evacuation when required.

What can be covered

Hospitalisation

Cover for inpatient treatment, including hospital stays, surgery, intensive care, specialist fees and prescribed medication while admitted.

Outpatient Care

Cover for everyday medical treatment such as doctor visits, specialist consultations, diagnostic tests, laboratory work, X-rays and prescribed medication.

Emergency Care & Evacuation

Protection for emergency treatment, ambulance services and, where included, medical evacuation to an appropriate medical facility.

Maternity

Selected plans can include prenatal care, delivery, postnatal treatment and pregnancy-related complications, with newborn cover available under some policies.

Dental & Optical

Optional benefits may include routine dental treatment, fillings and extractions, as well as eye examinations and allowances for prescription glasses or lenses.

Preventive Care & Wellness

Some plans also include health screenings, vaccinations and ongoing support for certain chronic conditions.

choose your IPMI plan

Three levels of
international health insurance

A - Hospitalisation + Medical Evacuation

This is the most straightforward level of private health insurance. It protects you against the cost of serious illness, accidents or medical conditions requiring hospital admission: inpatient treatment such as surgery, hospital accommodation, intensive care and other eligible hospital expenses. Medical evacuation is included as standard in the plans we offer, giving you an essential safety net should the treatment you need not be available locally.

Outpatient consultations, routine doctor visits and prescriptions are generally not covered at this level.

Best suited to: people looking for essential protection against major medical expenses while keeping their insurance premium under control.

B - Comprehensive Health Insurance + Medical Evacuation

Should you want broader access to private healthcare, a comprehensive plan combines hospitalisation cover with outpatient treatment. Alongside inpatient care, your policy can cover visits to general practitioners and specialists, diagnostic examinations and prescribed medication. Depending on the insurer and level selected, additional benefits such as physiotherapy or mental health treatment may also be available.

Best suited to: people looking for essential protection against major medical expenses while keeping their insurance premium under control.

C - Comprehensive Health Insurance + Maternity + Medical Evacuation

Should you be planning to start or grow your family, maternity cover can be added to selected comprehensive plans. Depending on the policy, maternity benefits can include prenatal and postnatal care, normal delivery, Caesarean delivery and certain newborn or pregnancy-related complications. Maternity cover normally needs to be arranged in advance, so it's particularly important to discuss your plans with us before pregnancy.

Best suited to: individuals and couples planning a pregnancy who want access to private maternity care as part of their international health insurance.

we explain

Why medical evacuation matters in Cambodia

Medical evacuation is one of the most important elements of health insurance in Cambodia. Many conditions can be treated locally, but there are situations where the appropriate specialist, facility or treatment simply isn't available. Should this happen, medical evacuation cover arranges and pays for an eligible transfer to an appropriate medical facility, subject to the terms of your policy and medical approval from the insurer, with our local team on hand to help coordinate the process.

Without adequate insurance, an emergency medical evacuation can represent a very significant personal expense. That is why medical evacuation is included in every international health insurance solution offered through AG Insurance Broker.

Living in Cambodia is generally straightforward, until you need medical treatment. Quality private healthcare is available, but serious treatment can quickly become expensive, good medical care here comes at international prices, and the right hospital network can be the difference between a manageable bill and a financial shock. In some situations, you may also need to travel elsewhere in Southeast Asia for specialist care.<\/p>

That is why the right health insurance is about more than simply paying hospital bills. It is about knowing where you can be treated, what your insurer will actually cover, and what happens if the care you need isn't available locally \u2014 and having a broker on the ground who knows For 20 years, AG Insurance Broker has helped expatriates, individuals and families in Cambodia answer exactly those questions. We know the local hospital network, the doctors and the care pathways in detail, and we work only with established international insurers selected among the leaders in their market, solid, reliable and responsive solutions, backed by a local team on hand to facilitate pre-authorisations and reimbursements. All our solutions guarantee renewal, whatever your claims history.<\/p>

Our plans give you access to trusted local and regional hospital networks, structured across local, regional (Southeast Asia) and worldwide cover, including medical evacuation. Plans can include dependants and family cover and maternity options, with a claims process built around direct billing; so the clinics you actually use are paid directly by the insurer, rather than leaving you to fund treatment and reclaim it later.<\/p>

Depending on the plan you choose, your cover can include treatment in Cambodia<\/strong>, throughout Southeast Asia<\/strong> or worldwide<\/strong>, together with medical evacuation when item.title: Employees Staff Insurance
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
health insurance - corporate insurance

Employee Health Insurance in Cambodia

Providing health insurance is one of the most practical benefits a company can offer its employees.

For staff, it means easier access to private healthcare when they need it. For employers, it provides a structured way to support employee wellbeing while strengthening the overall benefits package offered by the company.

At AG Insurance Broker, we design Employee Health Insurance plans in Cambodia for businesses of different sizes, from small teams and growing SMEs to larger companies with Cambodian and expatriate employees.

Get a Free quote

Health insurance designed around your workforce

Every company is different, and every employee does not necessarily need the same level of cover. A business may want straightforward local hospitalisation cover for its entire workforce, while providing broader international medical insurance for senior management or expatriate employees.

Group health insurance can therefore be structured with different levels of benefits according to employee category, seniority or role. Depending on the insurer and programme selected, cover can include:

  • Hospitalisation and inpatient treatment
  • Outpatient consultations
  • Specialist visits
  • Diagnostic tests
  • Prescribed medication
  • Emergency treatment
  • Medical evacuation
  • Dental care
  • Optical benefits
  • Maternity options
  • Life and disability benefits

Spouses and dependent children may also be added to eligible plans.

This flexibility allows companies to provide meaningful employee benefits while keeping the overall insurance programme within budget.

Need to chat with us?

Local or international
medical cover

One of the first decisions when setting up an employee health insurance plan in Cambodia is where employees should be able to receive treatment.

Local Health Insurance

Local plans are generally designed around hospitals and clinics within Cambodia and can provide an effective solution for companies seeking essential medical protection for their employees.

They can be particularly suitable for larger local workforces or businesses looking for a practical healthcare benefit at a controlled cost.

Regional & International Health Insurance

Companies employing expatriates, senior managers or employees who travel regularly may prefer access to a broader medical network. International plans can provide treatment across Southeast Asia or worldwide, depending on the geographical area selected. They may also include medical evacuation if appropriate treatment is not available locally.

A company can combine different levels of cover within the same overall employee benefits strategy.

Local plans are generally designed around hospitals and clinics within Cambodia and can provide an effective solution for companies seeking essential medical protection for their employees.

They can be particularly suitable for larger local workforces or businesses looking for a practical healthcare benefit at a controlled cost.

Companies employing expatriates, senior managers or employees who travel regularly may prefer access to a broader medical network. International plans can provide treatment across Southeast Asia or worldwide, depending on the geographical area selected. They may also include medical evacuation if appropriate treatment is not available locally.

A company can combine different levels of cover within the same overall employee benefits strategy.

Get a quote

Your free employee health insurance quote

Please enable JavaScript in your browser to complete this form.
Name *

A benefit employees actually use

Employee benefits are most valuable when staff understand them and can actually use them. Health insurance provides employees with something tangible: access to medical treatment when they become sick or injured without having to face the full cost themselves.

For employers, offering private medical insurance can also strengthen the overall employment package when recruiting and retaining staff.

In Cambodia's competitive employment market, a well-designed health plan can help demonstrate that the company takes the wellbeing of its employees seriously.

 

Group Health Insurance for small and large companies

Corporate medical insurance is not reserved for multinational companies or businesses with hundreds of employees.

AG Cambodia can arrange group health insurance for organisations with different workforce sizes and structures.

Your programme can evolve as your company grows. Employees can be added or removed as teams change, and benefit levels can be reviewed during renewal as your needs and budget develop.

The objective is not simply to buy an insurance policy, but to create a health programme that remains practical for both employees and management.

Less administration for your HR team

Managing employee health insurance can quickly become another administrative task for HR.

New employees need to be enrolled. Departing employees need to be removed. Benefits need to be explained, documents collected and claims or hospital questions sometimes followed up with the insurer.

This is where having a local broker makes a difference.

AG Insurance Broker assists with the ongoing administration of your corporate health programme, including:

  • Employee enrolment

  • Policy amendments

  • Adding and removing employees

  • Renewal preparation

  • Coordination with insurers

  • Questions regarding benefits and eligibility

  • Claims assistance

Instead of your HR department having to deal with several different insurer contacts, AG Cambodia provides one local point of contact for the programme.

Health Insurance for Cambodian and Expatriate Employees

Companies with mixed local and international teams often need more than one level of medical insurance.

A Cambodian employee who primarily uses healthcare locally may not require the same geographical coverage as an expatriate executive who wants access to hospitals in Bangkok, Singapore or elsewhere internationally.

Rather than placing everyone into an unnecessarily expensive single plan, we can help structure different benefit levels while keeping the programme coordinated under one corporate insurance strategy.

This allows businesses to balance employee benefits, healthcare access and budget more effectively.

Why choose AG Insurance Broker?

Choosing an Employee Health Insurance plan is not simply about comparing premiums.

Hospital networks, annual limits, outpatient benefits, geographical coverage, deductibles, exclusions, maternity conditions and medical evacuation can make two apparently similar plans very different.

AG Insurance Broker has been operating in Cambodia since 2006.

As an insurance broker, we compare available solutions and help companies understand the differences before selecting a plan.

We can help you:

  • Assess the needs of your workforce

  • Compare local and international insurance solutions

  • Create different benefit levels where appropriate

  • Understand hospital networks and coverage limits

  • Manage employee enrolment and changes

  • Prepare renewals

  • Assist employees and HR teams with insurance questions

  • Provide support when claims occur

Your company therefore has both access to the insurance market and a local team available to help manage the programme after it has been put in place.

Build the right health plan for your employees

Whether you employ five people or manage a much larger workforce, the right solution starts with understanding your team.

Tell us:

  • How many employees you want to insure

  • Their approximate age range

  • Whether employees are Cambodian, expatriate or a combination of both

  • The level of healthcare you want to provide

  • Whether you need local, regional or worldwide cover

  • Your approximate budget

We can then compare suitable Employee Health Insurance options in Cambodia and help you build a programme that works for both your employees and your company.

Ask AG Insurance Broker for a quotation and let us compare the available plans for your team.

Benefits, hospital networks, eligibility, exclusions, geographical limits and policy conditions vary according to the insurer and plan selected.

    Employee benefits<\/strong> are most valuable when staff understand them and can actually use them. Health insurance provides employees with something tangible: access to medical treatment<\/strong> when they become sick or injured without having to face the full cost themselves.<\/p>

    For employers, offering private medical insurance can also strengthen the overall employment package<\/strong> when recruiting and retaining staff.<\/p>

    In Cambodia's competitive employment market, a well-designed health plan can help demonstrate that the company takes the wellbeing of its employees seriously.<\/p>","_margin":{"unit":"%","top":"0","right":"11","bottom":"0","left":"4","isLinked":false},"_margin_tablet":{"unit":"%","top":"","right":"","bottom":"","left":"","isLinked":true},"_margin_mobile":{"unit":"%","top":"","right":"","bottom":"","left":"","isLinked":true},"_element_width":"initial","_element_custom_width":{"unit":"%","size":70,"sizes":[]},"jedv_conditions":[{"_id":"8ab3ba8"}],"__globals__":{"text_color":"globals\/colors?id=569aa52"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false},{"id":"1d4c9dc","elType":"container","settings":{"flex_direction":"column","jedv_conditions":[{"_id":"78938d5"}],"hide_tablet":"hidden-tablet","hide_mobile":"hidden-mobile"},"elements":[{"id":"d8b757a","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

    \u00a0<\/p>

    Group Health Insurance for small and large companies<\/h2>

    Corporate medical insurance is not reserved for multinational companies or businesses with hundreds of employees.<\/p>

    AG Cambodia can arrange group health insurance<\/strong> for organisations with different workforce sizes and structures.<\/p>

    Your programme can evolve as your company grows. Employees can be added or removed as teams change, and benefit levels can be reviewed during renewal as your needs and budget develop.<\/p>

    The objective is not simply to buy an insurance policy, but to create a health programme that remains practical for both employees and management.<\/p>

    Less administration for your HR team<\/h2>

    Managing employee health insurance can quickly become another administrative task for HR.<\/p>

    New employees need to be enrolled. Departing employees need to be removed. Benefits need to be explained, documents collected and claims or hospital questions sometimes followed up with the insurer.<\/p>

    This is where having a local broker makes a difference.<\/p>

    AG Insurance Broker assists with the ongoing administration of your corporate health programme, including:<\/p>

    • Employee enrolment<\/p><\/li>

    • Policy amendments<\/p><\/li>

    • Adding and removing employees<\/p><\/li>

    • Renewal preparation<\/p><\/li>

    • Coordination with insurers<\/p><\/li>

    • Questions regarding benefits and eligibility<\/p><\/li>

    • Claims assistance<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

      Instead of your HR department having to deal with several different insurer contacts, AG Cambodia provides one local point of contact for the programme.<\/strong><\/p>

      Health Insurance for Cambodian and Expatriate Employees<\/h2>

      Companies with mixed local and international teams often need more than one level of medical insurance.<\/p>

      A Cambodian employee who primarily uses healthcare locally may not require the same geographical coverage as an expatriate executive who wants access to hospitals in Bangkok, Singapore or elsewhere internationally.<\/p>

      Rather than placing everyone into an unnecessarily expensive single plan, we can help structure different benefit levels while keeping the programme coordinated under one corporate insurance strategy.<\/p>

      This allows businesses to balance employee benefits, healthcare access and budget<\/strong> more effectively.<\/p>

      Why choose AG Insurance Broker?<\/h2>

      Choosing an Employee Health Insurance plan is not simply about comparing premiums.<\/p>

      Hospital networks, annual limits, outpatient benefits, geographical coverage, deductibles, exclusions, maternity conditions and medical evacuation can make two apparently similar plans very different.<\/p>

      AG Insurance Broker has been operating in Cambodia since 2006.<\/strong><\/p>

      As an insurance broker, we compare available solutions and help companies understand the differences before selecting a plan.<\/p>

      We can help you:<\/p>

      • Assess the needs of your workforce<\/p><\/li>

      • Compare local and international insurance solutions<\/p><\/li>

      • Create different benefit levels where appropriate<\/p><\/li>

      • Understand hospital networks and coverage limits<\/p><\/li>

      • Manage employee enrolment and changes<\/p><\/li>

      • Prepare renewals<\/p><\/li>

      • Assist employees and HR teams with insurance questions<\/p><\/li>

      • Provide support when claims occur<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

        Your company therefore has both access to the insurance market and a local team available to help manage the programme after it has been put in place.<\/p>

        Build the right health plan for your employees<\/h2>

        Whether you employ five people or manage a much larger workforce, the right solution starts with understanding your team.<\/p>

        Tell us:<\/p>

        • How many employees you want to insure<\/p><\/li>

        • Their approximate age range<\/p><\/li>

        • Whether employees are Cambodian, expatriate or a combination of both<\/p><\/li>

        • The level of healthcare you want to provide<\/p><\/li>

        • Whether you need local, regional or worldwide cover<\/p><\/li>

        • Your approximate budget<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

          We can then compare suitable Employee Health Insurance options in Cambodia<\/strong> and help you build a programme that works for both your employees and your company.<\/p>

          Ask AG Insurance Broker for a quotation and let us compare the available plans for your team.<\/strong><\/p>

          Benefits, hospital networks, eligibility, exclusions, geographical limits and policy conditions vary according to the insurer and plan selected.<\/em><\/p>","jedv_conditions":[{"_id":"290f3ad"}]},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false}]

item.title: Vehicle Insurance: from motorbikes to SUV
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
PRIVATE INSURANCE - MOTOR VEHICLE COVERGAE

Vehicle Insurance

Driving in Cambodia comes with everyday risks, from minor accidents and vehicle damage to more serious collisions involving passengers or third parties. Private Vehicle Insurance can protect your car or scooter against accidental damage, theft and liability for injury or damage caused to others.

Depending on the level of cover selected, policies can include third-party liability, passenger liability and All Risks protection for your own vehicle. AG Cambodia can help you compare the available options and choose cover suited to your vehicle, how you use it and the level of protection you want.

item.title: Property Insurance
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
general insurance - private insurance

Home & Private Property Insurance

Our Home & Private Property Insurance provides comprehensive protection for your house or apartment, covering the value of your property together with your furniture, household equipment and personal belongings.

The policy can be arranged on an All Risks basis, offering broad protection against accidental loss or damage, including fire, water damage, natural events and theft, subject to the terms, conditions and exclusions of the policy.

The cover also includes Public Liability, protecting you against your legal liability towards third parties in connection with your property, including damage caused by the spread of fire to neighbouring properties, as well as accidental bodily injury or property damage involving visitors or other third parties.

Coverage can be tailored to the type and value of your property and is available for both private houses and apartments.

Get a Free quote

Get a quote

Your free Property insurance quote

Ask us for a quotation and we will help you identify the right level of protection for your home, apartment or rental property in Cambodia.

item.title: Public Liability
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
general insurance - private insurance

Public Liability

Public Liability responds when your business is held legally responsible for bodily injury or property damage caused to third party. It is not a risk reserved for shops, restaurants or offices that welcome the public, a factory, a workshop, a warehouse, a logistics site, a professional practice, or a contractor working on someone else's premises carries exactly the same exposure, the moment its people, its vehicles, its equipment or its products cause harm to a visitor, a neighbour, a supplier, or another company's staff. In practice, this exposure exists for virtually every type of business, regardless of sector or size.

Legal defence costs, compensation awards and medical expenses can escalate quickly and outpace what most businesses can absorb from cash flow alone. Public Liability transfers that risk to the insurer, and is included as standard in the business packages we design — from a single retail unit to an industrial site.

item.title: Construction risks
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
general insurance - business insurance

Contractor's All Risks Insurance (CAR)

Building a project exposes its full value — structure, materials, plant and equipment — from the day the first delivery reaches site. Contractor's All Risks (CAR) is placed as a single contract with two sections: material damage to the works, and third-party liability arising from the works.

The material damage section covers physical loss or damage to the permanent and temporary works, materials and site installations, as well as the contractor's plant and machinery, from any cause not specifically excluded — including fire, typhoon, flood and earthquake, covered as standard rather than sold as a costly extension. Extensions are available to carry cover through the defects-liability period, or to include existing structures affected by renovation works.

The liability section responds when the works cause bodily injury or property damage to a third party. Cambodian law requires every construction project to carry this liability cover — one of only two general insurance obligations in the country, together with liability cover for company vehicles. In practice, insurers issue material damage and liability cover together, as one policy, so the project and everyone around it are protected from the same day.

item.title: Marine cargo insurance in Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
general insurance - corporate insurance

Marine cargo Insurance

Goods lose the protection of four walls the moment they leave the warehouse. Marine Cargo insurance covers shipments, by sea, air or road, against loss or damage in transit, written on an all-risk basis under standard Institute Cargo Clauses wording, and covering loss, theft, breakage and water damage from the point of departure to final delivery.

Cover is typically arranged for the commercial value of the goods plus freight and duties, on a single-shipment or an annual open-cover basis for businesses shipping regularly. It's standard practice for importers, exporters, manufacturers, traders and freight forwarders moving goods in or out of Cambodia, and a condition frequently attached to letters of credit and supplier contracts.

item.title: A propos de AG Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
A propos

Assurance depuis 2006

Télécharger notre Profil (en Anglais)

Fondée et dirigée par David Tréal, AG Cambodge a été la toute première agence d'assurance agréée du Royaume et, depuis 17 ans, nous avons fourni des solutions d'assurance à quelques 3 000 familles, et traité avec succès autant de sinistres et de dossiers.

L'agence s'est développée en une solide équipe d'experts, dont les membres sont, soit spécialisés dans l'assurance santé expatrié sur mesure, soit dans les solutions d'assurance à usage général. Ils sont tous efficacement formés et hautement dévoués pour vous apporter une tranquillité d’esprit implacable.

Parce que nous avons une bonne compréhension de l’environnement médical actuel du pays, des risques inhérents à ce pays subtropical et de la façon dont les expatriés ont tendance à vivre leur vie, nous avons créé des modules d’assurance spéciaux pour respecter tout ce qui précède.

De plus, nous recherchons sans cesse de nouvelles solutions d’assurance, de nouveaux services mais aussi de meilleurs tarifs.

Notre bureau principal est situé au rez-de-chaussée de l'hôtel Himawari, qui offre de nombreux parkings pour un accès facile. Nous sommes ouverts du lundi au vendredi de 9h00 à 18h00. Pour les sinistres, nous mettrons à votre disposition un numéro d'urgence 24h/24, car nous serons à vos côtés et vous assisterons 24h/24.

Nous vous souhaitons tous un très beau séjour au Cambodge !

Fondée et dirigée par David Tréal, AG Cambodge a été la toute première agence d'assurance agréée du Royaume et, depuis 17 ans, nous avons fourni des solutions d'assurance à quelques 3 000 familles, et traité avec succès autant de sinistres et de dossiers.

L'agence s'est développée en une solide équipe d'experts, dont les membres sont, soit spécialisés dans l'assurance santé expatrié sur mesure, soit dans les solutions d'assurance à usage général. Ils sont tous efficacement formés et hautement dévoués pour vous apporter une tranquillité d’esprit implacable.

Parce que nous avons une bonne compréhension de l’environnement médical actuel du pays, des risques inhérents à ce pays subtropical et de la façon dont les expatriés ont tendance à vivre leur vie, nous avons créé des modules d’assurance spéciaux pour respecter tout ce qui précède.

De plus, nous recherchons sans cesse de nouvelles solutions d’assurance, de nouveaux services mais aussi de meilleurs tarifs.

Notre bureau principal est situé au rez-de-chaussée de l'hôtel Himawari, qui offre de nombreux parkings pour un accès facile. Nous sommes ouverts du lundi au vendredi de 9h00 à 18h00. Pour les sinistres, nous mettrons à votre disposition un numéro d'urgence 24h/24, car nous serons à vos côtés et vous assisterons 24h/24.

Nous vous souhaitons tous un très beau séjour au Cambodge !

item.title: Construction tous risques
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Devis en ligne

Les risques associés à la construction tels que le feu, la tempête, le vol, le vandalisme et bien d’autres sont couverts. La couverture Chantier Tous Risques inclut la Responsabilité Civile pour tout dommage accidentel aux tiers. En outre, ces polices d’assurance ne couvrent pas les accidents et les blessures des ouvriers sur le lieu de travail.

La couverture doit être effective avant le début du chantier, et prendre fin dés lors que les travaux sont terminés et que la propriété est prête à être utilisée ou occupée. Il est alors conseillé de souscrire une assurance Incendie permanente sur le bâtiment. La couverture Chantier Tous Risques est la seule garantie obligatoire au Cambodge controlée par les autorités.

item.title: Marc Delvallée: AG Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Insurance in Siem Reap

Marc Delvallée

Your Trusted Insurance Advisor in Siem Reap +855 81 545 473 Telegram Email

Navigating Insurance with a Personal Touch

Welcome to AG Insurance Broker, where we prioritize your peace of mind. Meet Marc Delvallée, our dedicated Business Development Manager based in Siem Reap. With years of experience in the insurance industry, Marc is here to guide you through the complexities of securing the right coverage for you and your loved ones.

Why work with Marc?

Expertise in Expatriate Insurance Needs

As an expatriate himself, Marc understands the unique challenges and requirements of living in Cambodia. He specializes in tailoring insurance solutions that cater to the diverse needs of expats, ensuring you have the right protection no matter where you are in the country.

A Client-Centered
Approach

As an expatriate himself, Marc understands the unique challenges and requirements of living in Cambodia. He specializes in tailoring insurance solutions that cater to the diverse needs of expats, ensuring you have the right protection no matter where you are in the country.

Local Knowledge,
Global Standards

Living in Siem Reap, Marc has in-depth knowledge of the local landscape. Combined with AG Cambodia's adherence to international insurance standards, this ensures you receive top-quality service and products that meet global expectations while being tailored to the Cambodian context. Mao Chanleakhena★★★★★ We have been with AG Cambodia since 2020, AG team is quick response with good service and support. Dylan Rogers★★★★★ Marc is so kind and thoughtful, he dropped into our office to explain all of the policy terms and conditions in person and his team is also very responsive and eager to help.Thank you for your service🙏 Sotheara Thach★★★★★ Prise en charge depuis 10 ans par AG, Très bon suivi pour les expates. A recommander. Rithy Sang★★★★★ I would like to express my gratitude to AG Cambodia for assisting me in obtaining insurance for my Schengen visa. Marc provided a tailored solution, and the team in Phnom Penh assured me that I could rely on their support in case of hospitalization in Europe. Thank you for the peace of mind that comes with being insured through AG Insurance Broker. Ciaran O' hEalai★★★★★ Je tiens aujourdhui a remercier AG Cambodia et surtout Marc qui nous a grandement aidé apres notre accident de route. Accident qui a engendré de nombreuses procedures medicales dont plusiers chirurgies mais egalement tout un tas de papraz!
  • marc@agcambodia.com
  • +855 81 545 473
  • Telegram

Health Insurance

Compare local and international health insurance plans tailored to life in Cambodia. Ask for a quote

Vehicle Insurance

Get the right coverage for your car or motorbike with trusted insurance providers. Ask for a quote

Travel Insurance

Travel with peace of mind—insurance for short trips, long stays, or expat journeys. Ask for a quote

Property Insurance

Protect your home, condo, or investment property in Cambodia from unexpected risks. Ask for a quote https://n8n.srv873866.hstgr.cloud/webhook/9c149560-3ed1-40a4-841d-2e214d0aa47a/chat

item.title: Glossary - Terms explained
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
A

  • Accident – An unforeseen and unintentional event resulting in injury, loss, or damage.
  • Act of God – A natural event (such as floods, earthquakes, or storms) that is beyond human control and not caused by negligence.
  • Actual Cash Value (ACV) – The value of an insured item at the time of loss, taking depreciation into account.
  • Adjuster (Claims Adjuster) – A professional who assesses insurance claims to determine the amount the insurer should pay.
  • Agent – A person or company authorized to sell insurance policies on behalf of an insurer.
  • Annuitant – The person who receives payments from an annuity contract.
  • Annual Limit – The maximum amount an insurance policy will pay for covered claims in a given year.
  • Applicant – The person or entity applying for an insurance policy.
  • Assessor – A professional who evaluates property damage and loss for insurance purposes.
  • Asset – Any valuable property or resource that an individual or business owns and can insure.
  • Assurance – A term often used interchangeably with "insurance," particularly in life insurance.
  • Auto Insurance – Coverage that protects against financial loss from vehicle-related accidents or damages.

B

  • Beneficiary – The person or entity designated to receive benefits from an insurance policy.
  • Binder – A temporary insurance contract providing coverage until the final policy is issued.
  • Bodily Injury Liability – Coverage that pays for injuries caused to others in an accident where the insured is at fault.
  • Broker – An independent professional who helps clients find and purchase insurance policies from various insurers.
  • Burglary Insurance – Coverage that protects against losses resulting from theft or burglary.
  • Business Interruption Insurance – Coverage that compensates businesses for lost income due to unexpected disruptions like fires or natural disasters.

C

  • Cancellation – The termination of an insurance policy before its expiration date.
  • Capitation – A payment model where a healthcare provider is paid a fixed amount per patient rather than per service.
  • Claim – A formal request by an insured person for compensation due to a covered loss.
  • Co-insurance – The percentage of costs the insured must pay after meeting the deductible.
  • Comprehensive Coverage – Insurance that covers damages to an insured vehicle from non-collision events (theft, fire, natural disasters, etc.).
  • Coverage – The specific protection provided by an insurance policy.
  • Critical Illness Insurance – A policy that pays a lump sum if the insured is diagnosed with a serious illness like cancer or heart disease.

D

  • Deductible – The amount an insured must pay out of pocket before the insurer covers a claim.
  • Depreciation – The decrease in the value of an insured asset over time.
  • Disability Insurance – Coverage that provides income if the insured becomes unable to work due to illness or injury.
  • Double Indemnity – A life insurance clause that pays twice the policy amount if death occurs under specific circumstances, such as an accident.

E

  • Endorsement (Rider) – An amendment to an insurance policy that modifies its coverage.
  • Exclusion – A specific condition or circumstance that is not covered by an insurance policy.
  • Excess (Deductible) – The amount an insured must pay before the insurer covers the rest of the claim.
  • Expiration Date – The date an insurance policy ends unless renewed.

F

  • Face Value – The amount payable upon the maturity of a life insurance policy or upon the insured's death.
  • First-Party Coverage – Insurance that covers the policyholder’s own losses, rather than third-party claims.
  • Flood Insurance – A policy that covers damages caused by flooding, typically not included in standard homeowner’s insurance.

G

  • Grace Period – A period after a missed payment during which an insurance policy remains active.
  • Group Insurance – A single insurance policy covering a group of people, such as employees of a company.

H

  • Hazard – Any condition that increases the likelihood of an insurance loss.
  • Health Insurance – Coverage that pays for medical expenses incurred by the insured.
  • Homeowners Insurance – A policy that protects a home and its contents from risks such as fire, theft, and liability.
  • Hospital Cash Plan – A type of health insurance that provides a daily cash benefit for hospital stays.

I - J - K

  • Indemnity – Compensation paid to restore an insured party to their financial position before a loss.
  • Insurable Interest – A financial or personal interest in the insured item or person that would cause financial loss if damaged or deceased.
  • Insurance Policy – A contract between the insurer and the insured detailing coverage, terms, and conditions.
  • Insured – The person or entity covered by an insurance policy.
  • Insurer – The insurance company that provides coverage and pays claims.
  • Joint Life Insurance – A life insurance policy covering two people, usually spouses.
  • Key Person Insurance – A policy covering a crucial employee whose loss would financially impact a business.

L

  • Liability – Legal responsibility for damages or injuries to others.
  • Life Insurance – A policy that provides financial compensation upon the insured’s death.
  • Lapse – Termination of a policy due to non-payment of premiums.
  • Long-Term Care Insurance – Coverage for extended medical and personal care needs.

M - N - O

  • Marine Insurance – Coverage for ships, cargo, and marine liabilities.
  • Maturity Date – The date when an insurance policy’s benefits become payable.
  • Moral Hazard – The increased likelihood of risky behavior due to having insurance coverage.
  • Named Insured – The primary person covered under a policy.
  • No-Claim Bonus – A discount for not making claims during a policy period.
  • Occupational Hazard – Workplace risks that can impact insurance coverage and premiums.

P - Q - R - S

  • Policyholder – The person who owns an insurance policy.
  • Premium – The amount paid for an insurance policy.
  • Public Liability Insurance – Coverage for injuries or damages caused to third parties.
  • Reinsurance – When an insurer transfers part of its risk to another insurance company.
  • Subrogation – The insurer’s right to recover claim costs from a third party responsible for the loss.

T - U - V - W - X - Y - Z

  • Term Insurance – A life insurance policy that provides coverage for a fixed period.
  • Third-Party Insurance – Coverage that pays for damages to others but not the insured’s own losses.
  • Underwriting – The process of evaluating risks and determining insurance terms.
  • Waiting Period – The time before certain policy benefits take effect.

item.title: ACS - Health Insurance
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
ACS Expat Health Insurance

Comprehensive international health coverage designed for expatriates and long-term travelers. Customize your protection with a modular approach that fits your lifestyle and your budget — starting with essential hospitalization and evacuation, then adding outpatient care, dental, maternity, and more as needed. Download the spec sheet

Core Coverage

Hospitalisation & Medevac

Every ACS Expat plan includes this essential module by default.

  • Coverage for hospital stays over 24 hours
  • Surgical procedures, ICU, and prescribed treatments
  • Private room (limit varies by plan level)
  • Cancer treatment (limits depend on the plan)
  • Psychiatric hospitalization (after a 3-month waiting period)
  • Organ transplants (excluding donor and related medication costs)
  • Medical evacuation to the nearest suitable medical center
  • Return transport to your country of residence after treatment
  • Rehabilitation, hospital-at-home, and local ambulance
  • Emergency hospitalization while traveling outside your covered zone (short trips only)

Optional Modules

Routine Medical Care (Outpatient)

Covers everyday healthcare needs like:

  • General practitioner and specialist visits
  • Laboratory tests, scans, and MRIs
  • Prescription medication and vaccines
  • Physiotherapy and alternative medicine (e.g., acupuncture)
  • Cancer screening and general health checkups
  • Self-medication and smoking cessation (Level 2+)

Levels available:

  • Level 1 (basic outpatient care)
  • Level 2 (extended coverage)
  • Level 3 (comprehensive, Platinum-only)

Dental & Optical

Available only if you subscribe to outpatient care.

  • Dental cleanings, fillings, extractions, root canals
  • Dental prosthetics (inlays, crowns, implants)
  • Orthodontics (children under 16)
  • Prescription glasses and contact lenses
  • Laser vision correction

Two levels:

  • Level 1: up to €/$2,000 per year
  • Level 2: up to €/$4,000 per year

Maternity

Requires outpatient module. 12-month waiting period.

  • Pre- and post-natal consultations
  • Hospital delivery and private room
  • Caesarean section (if medically required)
  • Childbirth preparation
  • Newborn screening and care
  • Medically Assisted Reproduction (Level 2 only, 18-month wait)

Two levels:

  • Level 1: up to €/$6,000 per pregnancy
  • Level 2: up to €/$12,000 per pregnancy

Assistance Plus

Extra support benefits for real-life emergencies:

  • Hotel costs post-Medevac (€/$80 per night up to 10 nights)
  • Childcare during hospitalization
  • Early return tickets in case of family emergency
  • Repatriation of family members
  • Legal support and psychological assistance
  • Funeral expenses and body transport
  • Search and rescue costs

Need more information about ACS?

Chat with Marc English | Français

Plan Levels Comparison

Plan Annual Limit Private Room Limit Cancer Treatment Coverage
Bronze €/$500,000 €/$100 per day Not covered
Silver €/$1,000,000 €/$150 per day Up to €/$3,000 per year
Gold €/$2,000,000 €/$250 per day Up to €/$3,500 per year
Platinum €/$3,000,000 100% of actual cost Up to €/$4,000 per year

item.title: Medevac - Medical Evacuation from Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
MEDICAL EVACUATION

in Cambodia

When every second counts, peace of mind begins with a plan. From ground ambulances in Phnom Penh to international airlifts across borders, medical evacuation ensures you get the care you need — wherever you are. READ MORE

What is Medevac?

Medical Evacuation and Why It Matters

Medevac is short for medical evacuation

An essential emergency service designed to transport a patient from the scene of a serious illness or injury to a healthcare facility that can provide the necessary level of care.

In Cambodia and across the region, this often means:
  • A ground ambulance transfer from your home, hotel, or local clinic to a larger hospital
  • Coordination and admission to a better-equipped facility, either domestically or internationally
  • In more severe or remote cases, a helicopter or fixed-wing air ambulance to a neighboring country like Thailand, Vietnam, or Singapore
  • While many private hospitals in Cambodia do have their own ambulances, this local transport is just the first link in the chain.

A complete Medevac operation can include:

  • Emergency medical teams
  • Air transfer with on-board monitoring
  • Landing rights, visas, and hospital bed reservations
  • Repatriation back to your country of residence after stabilization

Medevac is more than transportation
it’s an emergency logistics solution designed to save lives when time and distance matter most.

Medical Air Service Air
Air ambulance, repatriation to/from Cambodia, intensive care transport, infectious disease containment. Website
Helistar Cambodia
search and rescue, coordination with ground medical teams. Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, regional Website
Helitop Cambodia
Helitop Aviation Air ambulance, medical rescue, helicopter charter, strategic partnerships. Phnom Penh-based Click here
Air Ambulance Worldwide
Royal Phnom Penh Hospital Emergency ground ambulance, air evacuation team for international transfers. Phnom Penh Click here
Horizon Air Ambulance
Horizon Air Ambulance 24-hour worldwide air medical flights to/from Cambodia, full logistics support. Click here

Page Title (H1):
What is Medevac?
Understanding Emergency Medical Evacuation and Why It Matters

Section 1 (H2):
What Does “Medevac” Mean?
Define “Medevac” (short for “medical evacuation”)

Explain that it refers to emergency transport to a capable medical facility

Mention that it often involves air ambulances, especially across borders

Section 2 (H2):
Why Is Medevac So Important?
Talk about being abroad in a place without adequate medical care

Explain how Medevac can be life-saving in time-critical situations

Add an emotional hook or short real-life scenario (optional)

Section 3 (H2):
What Does Medevac Typically Include?
Use bullet points:

Medical assessment and coordination

Ground transport to/from airports

Flight in a medical aircraft if needed

Onboard doctor or nurse

Admission into a qualified hospital

Repatriation after treatment

Section 4 (H2):
Do All Insurance Plans Cover Medevac?
Briefly say that not all do — especially budget or basic plans

Emphasize the importance of checking

Suggest what to look for:

24/7 access

Global reach

No hidden limitations

Section 5 (H2):
Who Needs Medevac Coverage?
Expatriates

Long-term travelers

Remote workers / digital nomads

Anyone traveling to areas with limited medical infrastructure

Section 6 (H2):
Final Thought
Reiterate that Medevac isn’t a luxury — it’s protection

Use a human tone: “You hope you never need it. But if you do…”

End with a call to awareness or action:
“Check your plan. Know your options. Protect your future.”

Page Title (H1):
What is Medevac?
Understanding Emergency Medical Evacuation and Why It Matters

Section 1 (H2):
What Does “Medevac” Mean?
Define “Medevac” (short for “medical evacuation”)

Explain that it refers to emergency transport to a capable medical facility

Mention that it often involves air ambulances, especially across borders

Section 2 (H2):
Why Is Medevac So Important?
Talk about being abroad in a place without adequate medical care

Explain how Medevac can be life-saving in time-critical situations

Add an emotional hook or short real-life scenario (optional)

Section 3 (H2):
What Does Medevac Typically Include?
Use bullet points:

Medical assessment and coordination

Ground transport to/from airports

Flight in a medical aircraft if needed

Onboard doctor or nurse

Admission into a qualified hospital

Repatriation after treatment

Section 4 (H2):
Do All Insurance Plans Cover Medevac?
Briefly say that not all do — especially budget or basic plans

Emphasize the importance of checking

Suggest what to look for:

24/7 access

Global reach

No hidden limitations

Section 5 (H2):
Who Needs Medevac Coverage?
Expatriates

Long-term travelers

Remote workers / digital nomads

Anyone traveling to areas with limited medical infrastructure

Section 6 (H2):
Final Thought
Reiterate that Medevac isn’t a luxury — it’s protection

Use a human tone: “You hope you never need it. But if you do…”

End with a call to awareness or action:
“Check your plan. Know your options. Protect your future.”

item.title: APRIL - Health Insurance
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
APRIL Expat Health Insurance

Comprehensive, flexible global health coverage — tailor-made for expats, long-term travelers, and remote workers. Download the spec sheet

Core Coverage

Hospitalisation & Medevac

Every APRIL  plan includes this essential module by default.

  • Emergency & accident hospitalisation (100% of actual/reasonable costs)

  • Two-bed or standard private rooms (between 75–100 USD daily, depending on plan)

  • Medical repatriation included in every plan.

  • No cash advance for hospital stays with prior approval

Additional

Module Options

Outpatient Care – GP and specialist consultations, testing and diagnostics

Vision & Dental – Included only with outpatient; coverage tiers vary by plan

Maternity – Optional with outpatient; coverage up to 3,000 USD (Essential), 6,000 USD (Comfort), 12,000 USD (Premium)

Coverage Zones & Travel

Select a Cover Zone based on primary country of residence:

  • Zone 1 – Cambodia + most world (excl. US, Japan, etc.)

  • Zone 2 & 3 – Broader geographical scope — see brochure 

Temporary travel (<90 days) outside your zone permitted (accident/medical emergency

Deductibles & Premium Adjustments

Choose an annual deductible that fits your needs:

  • Options typically: 500 USD, 1,000 USD, 2,500 USD, 5,000 USD
  • Choosing a higher deductible lowers the premium

Digital Advantage & Service

  • 100% paperless enrolment and reimbursement via EasyClaim app 

  • 24/7 teleconsultation and multilingual support via chat or app 

  • No hospital upfront billing (with prior approval)

Need more information about APRIL?

Chat with Marc English | Français APRIL Coverage Levels

Coverage Levels (Plans)

Plan Annual Limit Hospitalisation Room
Emergency 250,000 USD Two-bed (accident/emergency only)
Basic 500,000 USD Two-bed or standard private
Essential 1,000,000 USD Private room up to 75 USD/day
Comfort 1,500,000 USD Standard private room
Premium Unlimited Standard private room
Premium and Comfort may include higher ceilings or denials depending on zone

item.title: LUMA - Health Insurance
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
LUMA Expat Health Insurance

Comprehensive, customizable health insurance — designed for expats and families in Cambodia and across Asia. Download the spec sheet

Core Coverage

Hospitalisation & Medevac

  • Inpatient and day-case hospitalisation

  • Private room up to USD 170/day (Superior care and above cover true private rooms) 

  • Emergency evacuation & repatriation worldwide (within zone)

  • Direct billing with network hospitals, both inpatient and outpatient 

  • Locally applicable from Day 1

Additional

Module Options

  • Outpatient & routine health checks (GP visits, diagnostic tests)

  • Dental & Vision (check-ups, major dental work, glasses)

  • Maternity (normal delivery and complications – with waiting period) These follow the same modular structure noted in Plans 4 and 5

Coverage Zones & Travel

  • Residence requirement: 185+ days/year in Cambodia 

  • Area of cover: Choose Zone A/B/C (Zone C is worldwide excluding major countries) 

  • Emergency cover worldwide: Up to 60-day trips outside zone, capped at USD 250 000/year

Deductibles & Premium Adjustments

Optional deductibles available:

  1. USD 0
  2. USD 500
  3. USD 1 000
  4. USD 6 000

Digital Advantage & Service

  • Age eligibility: 0–70 (must apply with parent if under 18) 
  • Renewable for life, regardless of age or health condition 
  • Free choice of hospital, wide direct-billing network 
  • Digital support: Mobile app, 24/7 member care, claim tracking

Need more information about LUMA?

Chat with Marc English | Français

🔹 Plan Levels at a Glance

Plan Annual Limit Hospitalisation Room
Plan 1 – Essential Care USD 1,000,000 Private room up to USD 170/day
Plan 2 – Balance Care USD 1,000,000 Private room up to USD 170/day
Plan 3 – Superior Care USD 1,000,000 Private room up to USD 170/day
Plan 4 – Premium Care USD 1,600,000 Full private room (paid in full)
Plan 5 – Platinum Care USD 1,600,000 Full private room (paid in full)

item.title: Policy
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Privacy & Data Use Policy

Last updated: September 2025

At AG Cambodia, we value your privacy and are committed to protecting the personal information you share with us. This policy explains how we collect, use, and safeguard your data when you interact with our website, request a quote, or submit a lead form.

1. Information We Collect

When you use our website or submit a lead form, we may collect:

Name, email address, and phone number

Information about your insurance needs (e.g., type of coverage, family size, age)

Any other details you choose to provide in your message

2. How We Use Your Information

We use the information you provide to:

Respond to your inquiries and provide insurance quotes

Recommend the most suitable insurance products and services

Contact you about your request or related services

Improve our website and services

We will never sell or rent your personal information to third parties.

3. Data Sharing

Your data may be shared only with:

Trusted insurance partners for the purpose of providing accurate quotes and policies

Service providers who help us manage our website and communications

All partners are required to maintain strict confidentiality.

4. Data Security

We take appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect your personal information from unauthorized access, loss, misuse, or disclosure.

5. Cookies & Tracking

Our website uses cookies and analytics tools (such as Google Analytics and Meta Pixel) to understand visitor behavior and improve our services. You can disable cookies in your browser settings.

6. Your Rights

You have the right to:

Access the personal data we hold about you

Request corrections or updates

Ask us to delete your data (unless required by law to keep it)

To exercise these rights, please contact us at:
📧 info@agcambodia.com

📞 +855 69 635 985 (Marie) or +855 81 545 473 (Marc)

7. Policy Updates

We may update this policy from time to time. Any changes will be posted on this page with the updated date.

item.title: Traffic in Cambodia. What you need to know
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded: Third Party Liability is the most critical risk as third party has usually the favor of authorities against foreigner car. Therefore in order to avoid high indemnity costs from Third party it is very important to be insuring your car while driving in Cambodia. In case of accident call immediately the insurer 24/7 hotline for assistance. Stay in your car and wait for the claim officer to assist you with the police and third party . Don’t be surprised if the police request to impound your car until the claim is resolved and closed . Therefore it may take several days before the insurer and third party reach an agreement and finally release your car. Roads are not what you would called "safe", and though there are lots of traffic laws, very few rules are actually enforced. Therefore you must be highly vigilant at all times while on, or near a road. You may end up in a hit and run accident when the third party runs away after hitting your vehicle, you can cover any damage to your car by Own Damage insurance , the insurer would pay your damage in a case of hit and run . For bodily damage it is best to be covered by Expatriate Health Insurance with high limits of cover and treatment available worldwide with evacuation. Driving licenses (car ,moto) : You must hold a Cambodian Valid Driving License to be covered by your motor insurance in Cambodia. Those holding a driving license from their origin country can get an equivalent Cambodian License by showing a copy to a Driving School. Driving school will charge a fee of about USD 50 in order to issue a one-year Cambodian Driving license . The license must be renewed each year for the same fee. Motorbike driving license is required for any motorbike with capacity greater than 125cc . In this case you may have an equivalent licence from your country of origin or you must pass the test in Cambodia . The fee is approximately US 250 to pass the license.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: How can you drive in Cambodia? Well, you need a driver's license and some awesome reflexes ! Anything and i mean anything can come from anywhere. This is true in the countryside but not less in the capital Phnom penh
Traffic and driving skills in Cambodia

item.title: Why should you insure your property?
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded: In Cambodia, as a tenant (lessee) you are legally responsible for any loss and damages occurring to the property of your landlord (lessor) - unless the lease agreement specifically states otherwise). Therefore, in order to avoid costly compensation from your ex-landlord, it is best to insure your apartment or business. The insurance premium should at least cover the construction value of the property. Of course you may want to include your personal belongings and the furniture and appliances. The insurance company will cover any loss and damage to property when it is caused by fire, explosion, windstorm, water & flood and even vehicle impact . If you are the owner of a property in Cambodia we would also strongly advice on insuring your investment. Whether it concerns a building, a house, a factory or a condominium, against the same accidents. Considering environment, where safety procedures and construction standards are not being enforced at all level, your property is at greatly at risk.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Considering the framework in Cambodia, one would seriously consider an insurance for its property, when the risk is very present.

item.title: Information On Health Insurance In Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded: [caption id="attachment_17" align="alignleft" width="200"] Insurance[/caption] Whether you have decided to relocate to the country Cambodia or you are in search of a new type of international health insurance, it is very important to know what is available in relation to insurance provisions as well as information on the country's facilities and medical care. Cambodia is a country with around 14,805,000 people and the estimated life expectancy is around 57 years for men and around 65 years for women. Healthcare in provincial areas in Cambodia especially in areas that border Laos is extremely poor and even though the major cities are better, the system is still struggling and dealing with a demand that remains constant. Health insurance in Cambodia is not up to the international standards but is slowly improving. So when you decide to relocate or travel to Cambodia it is vital that you make sure you have full coverage with personal or family health insurance. Healthcare Facilities Provinces in Cambodia experience what is considered to be extremely bad levels related to healthcare in this country. Ratanakiri is a province that experiences some of the worst types of regular endemic outbreaks such as intestinal parasites, malaria, measles, cholera and tuberculosis. These types of outbreaks are vaccine-preventable, but these types of areas experience a lack of medical attention and medicines. These diseases form a great contribution to mortality rates of pregnant women and children. These rural areas endure these types of issues due to factors that include poor accessibility to water and infrastructure, language and cultural barriers, physical remoteness and of course poverty. Other important factors related to poor health insurance in Cambodia are that medical supplies and equipment are extremely minimal. Many of their health facilities are run by staff that have been trained poorly as well as erratically paid.

item.title: Is the Water Festival a safe event?
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
The Water Festival, is a national event, taking place once a year, at the end of the raining season. It used to be a Phnom Penh event, as the King oversees the celebrations, but now has a sister event in Siem Reap. The main event is a boat racing, among districts and provinces.
This celebration draft people from all over the country, bringing thousands and sometimes millions to the Capital, turning the city into a giant fair. And as you would expect, very large crowds often brings troubles. In fact, Cambodia had suffered a national tragedy in 2014 with a massive stampede on a small narrow bridge, killing a few dozen teenagers in an horrible massacre. This catastrophe had put an end to the celebration for a couple of years, before coming back in 2016. But the government had drawn from this experience and has properly and efficiently grid the riverside with police patrols, emergency medical units and video cameras all along the riverside.
So is the Water Festival in Phnom penh a safe celebration? We would think it is now a perfectly safe for families, tourists and locals.

item.title: Naviguer dans les complexités de la mort au Cambodge : un guide complet
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Death is a challenging and inevitable part of life, and dealing with it in a foreign country adds layers of complexity. Cambodia, with its rich cultural heritage and distinct legal framework, has specific protocols and practices for handling death. Here’s a detailed guide to help you navigate this difficult process.

1. Preparation Before Death

Register with the Consulate: If you’re an expatriate living in Cambodia, it’s prudent to register with your respective consulate or embassy. This registration can facilitate communication and assistance in case of emergencies.

Inform Your Family: Clearly communicate your wishes regarding end-of-life arrangements with your family. This includes preferences for burial or cremation, repatriation of remains, and any specific rituals or ceremonies.

Insurance: Securing comprehensive health and life insurance that covers repatriation and other associated costs is essential. Verify that your insurance policy is valid in Cambodia and understand the coverage details.

Legal Arrangements: Consider consulting a local notary or legal expert to draft a will or other legal documents specifying your wishes. This step can prevent potential legal disputes and ensure your wishes are respected.

2. Immediate Steps After Death

Obtain a Death Certificate: The first and foremost step is to obtain a death certificate from a local hospital or the relevant Cambodian authorities. This document is crucial for all subsequent processes.

Notify the Embassy or Consulate: Contact the deceased’s embassy or consulate. They can provide guidance and support, including assisting with the necessary paperwork and informing the next of kin.

Inform the Insurance Company: Notify the deceased’s insurance company promptly. They will require a copy of the death certificate and other relevant documents to process any claims.

3. Handling the Remains

Repatriation or Local Burial: Decide whether the remains will be repatriated to the deceased’s home country or buried/cremated locally. Repatriation involves additional steps, including embalming and securing a coffin that meets international standards. The embassy can assist with these arrangements but note that the costs must be covered by the family.

Local Burial or Cremation: If the choice is to handle the remains locally, engage with local funeral services. Cambodia has numerous funeral service providers familiar with both local customs and the needs of expatriates.

4. Administrative Procedures

Report to Local Authorities: Report the death to the local Cambodian authorities, such as the police, especially if the death occurred outside of a medical facility. This step is necessary for legal documentation and any potential investigations.

Bank and Financial Accounts: Inform the relevant banks and financial institutions about the death. This notification helps in freezing accounts and preventing unauthorized transactions.

Property and Assets: If the deceased owned property or other significant assets in Cambodia, initiate the legal process for the transfer or disposal of these assets. This process might require the services of a local attorney.

5. Cultural Sensitivities and Support

Respect Local Customs: Cambodia has its own set of cultural practices and traditions regarding death and funerals. Engaging with local customs respectfully can ease the process and provide a sense of closure.

Seek Support: Don’t hesitate to seek emotional and logistical support from local expatriate communities, religious organizations, or grief counseling services.

Conclusion

Dealing with the death of a loved one is never easy, and doing so in a foreign country like Cambodia can be particularly daunting. However, with proper preparation, clear communication, and the right support, you can navigate this challenging time with greater ease. Ensure that you have all the necessary information and assistance by consulting with local authorities, your embassy, and legal experts.

For further details and specific procedural information, refer to the comprehensive guide by Le Petit Journal here.

item.title: Le Cambodge reste une destination sûre
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
🇰🇭 Le Cambodge reste une destination sûre – Mise à jour pour nos clients et partenaires

Le Cambodge demeure un pays sûr et accueillant pour les expatriés, les touristes et les résidents de long terme.

Bien que certaines tensions aient été signalées dans des zones frontalières isolées avec la Thaïlande, la vie quotidienne à Phnom Penh, Siem Reap ou Sihanoukville suit son cours normalement. Les déplacements, les activités économiques et les services ne sont pas affectés.

Nous recommandons simplement de : ✔️ Suivre les consignes des autorités locales et de votre ambassade
✔️ Éviter les zones frontalières sensibles sans nécessité absolue
✔️ S'enregistrer auprès des services consulaires pour les séjours prolongés

Chez AG Cambodia, votre sécurité et votre tranquillité d’esprit sont au cœur de notre mission. Que vous viviez ici ou que vous planifiiez un voyage, nous sommes à vos côtés pour vous informer, vous accompagner, et vous proposer la couverture d’assurance la plus adaptée.

📩 N’hésitez pas à nous contacter pour toute question ou besoin de conseil.

#AGCambodia #SécuritéCambodge #Expatriés #VoyagerSerein #AssuranceCambodge
