item.title: Visa Business ou Permit de travail
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Ce que les expatriés doivent savoir au Cambodge

(Édition 2025)

Si vous vivez au Cambodge en tant qu’expatrié — que vous soyez freelance, retraité avec un revenu complémentaire, ou salarié à distance — vous vous êtes probablement déjà demandé :
« Ai-je besoin d’un permis de travail ou un visa business suffit-il ? »

La réponse courte : les deux peuvent être nécessaires, selon votre situation et votre activité. Voici un tour d’horizon pour rester en conformité — et éviter les amendes ou problèmes de visa.

🛂 Le visa : votre point d’entrée

La majorité des étrangers travaillant ou générant un revenu au Cambodge entrent avec un visa de catégorie E (EB) — plus communément appelé visa business.
Ce visa n’est pas un permis de travail. Il vous autorise uniquement à séjourner légalement dans le pays pour une activité professionnelle ou commerciale.

📅 Durée :

  • Valable 30 jours à l’entrée

  • Peut être prolongé pour 1, 3, 6 ou 12 mois

  • Renouvelable sans limite

🏢 Le permis de travail : obligatoire pour la majorité

Un permis de travail est obligatoire en plus du visa dès que vous travaillez ou exercez une activité rémunérée au Cambodge.

Les permis sont délivrés en ligne via le portail du Ministère du Travail :
➡️ FWCMS

💸 Frais officiels :

  • 130 $ par an

  • (Attention : certaines agences peuvent facturer des frais de service supplémentaires)

📋 Documents requis :

  • Passeport valide et visa business

  • Justificatif d’emploi ou d’enregistrement d’entreprise

  • Approbation de l’employeur + respect du quota étranger

  • Certificat médical

⚠️ Oui, même les freelances et travailleurs à distance ont besoin d’un permis de travail, sauf dérogation spécifique (voir ci-dessous).

👨‍💻 Et les freelances ou télétravailleurs ?

Le Cambodge ne reconnaît pas officiellement le statut de travailleur indépendant.
Si vous travaillez seul (pour des clients à l’étranger ou sur place), vous êtes considéré comme travailleur indépendant et devez :

✅ Créer une entité légale (entreprise individuelle ou société)
✅ Obtenir un visa business
✅ Demander un permis de travail au nom de votre structure

💡 Conseil : Si vous facturez des clients au Cambodge ou à l’international, et que vous résidez dans le pays à long terme, vous êtes juridiquement considéré comme en activité professionnelle, même sans employeur local.

🧓 Retraités avec une activité annexe : êtes-vous concernés ?

Si vous êtes à la retraite mais que vous :

  • Offrez des services de conseil

  • Enseignez quelques heures par semaine

  • Animez une chaîne YouTube ou un blog monétisé
    Alors oui, vous êtes considéré comme actif économiquement au regard de la loi cambodgienne.

Dans ce cas, vous devez envisager :

  • Un visa business

  • Un permis de travail

  • Un enregistrement d’entreprise (si applicable)

⚠️ Les pensions de retraite seules ne nécessitent pas de permis de travail.

👔 Salarié d’une entreprise locale ?

Dans ce cas, l’employeur est responsable de :

  • Faire une demande de quota de travailleurs étrangers (max. 10 % de l’effectif)

  • Vous inscrire au système de sécurité sociale NSSF

  • Effectuer la demande annuelle de permis de travail

Répartition du quota :

  • 3 % : employés de bureau

  • 6 % : personnel qualifié

  • 1 % : personnel non qualifié

❌ Que se passe-t-il sans permis de travail ?

Les risques sont réels :

  • Amendes

  • Annulation de visa

  • Blocages sur les futurs renouvellements ou entrées

Les contrôles sont de plus en plus fréquents, notamment à Phnom Penh et Siem Reap.

🛡️ Cotisations de sécurité sociale (NSSF)

Si vous êtes salarié (ou dirigez une entreprise), vous devez également être enregistré auprès du Fonds National de Sécurité Sociale (NSSF).

Le NSSF couvre :

  • ✅ Assurance maladie

  • ✅ Accidents du travail

  • ✅ Cotisations retraite

📌 Depuis 2018, l’assurance santé est 100 % à la charge de l’employeur
📌 Les cotisations retraite ont commencé à 4 % du salaire (partagée entre employeur et salarié)

🏠 Le Visa “Golden” (CM2H) : une alternative ?

Si vous êtes investisseur, vous pouvez opter pour le visa CM2H “My Second Home” :

  • Investissement de 100 000 $ minimum

  • Visa valable 10 ans, renouvelable

  • Pas besoin de permis de travail

  • Possibilité de demander la citoyenneté après 5 ans

🎯 Solution idéale pour les investisseurs passifs ou les entrepreneurs ne souhaitant pas exercer d’activité salariée formelle.

item.title: Comprendre la résidence fiscale des étrangers au Cambodge
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Comprendre la résidence fiscale des étrangers au Cambodge

— Et pourquoi la déclaration est essentielle

1. Qui est considéré comme résident fiscal ?

Selon la législation fiscale cambodgienne, un individu étranger est considéré comme résident fiscal s’il remplit l’un des critères suivants :

  • Il est domicilié au Cambodge, ou

  • Il maintient son lieu de résidence principal au Cambodge, ou

  • Il est physiquement présent au Cambodge pendant plus de 182 jours au cours de toute période de 12 mois (sources : CBRE, Moore Global).

Une fois classé comme résident, un individu est imposé de manière progressive sur ses revenus mondiaux, contrairement au taux forfaitaire de 20 % appliqué aux non-résidents (CBRE).

Barèmes d’imposition pour les résidents (Impôt sur le salaire) :

  • 0 % sur les premiers ~1,5 million KHR/mois

  • 5 %, 10 %, 15 % sur les tranches suivantes

  • 20 % au-delà de 12,5 millions KHR/mois (sources : ASEAN Briefing, PwC Tax Summaries)

En comparaison, les non-résidents sont imposés à un taux forfaitaire de 20 % sur les salaires provenant du Cambodge, sans aucune déduction ni exonération (CBRE).

2. Déclaration de résidence : une obligation, pas un automatisme

Il est essentiel de comprendre que remplir les critères de résidence ne suffit pas pour bénéficier du régime fiscal progressif.

L’employé étranger et l’employeur doivent formellement déclarer et enregistrer le statut de résidence fiscale de l’individu auprès du Département général des impôts (GDT).

Cette déclaration est indispensable pour :

  • activer l’imposition progressive

  • bénéficier des avantages liés, comme les déductions pour personnes à charge

Ne pas déclarer peut entraîner la poursuite de l’imposition au taux forfaitaire de 20 %, même si les conditions de résidence sont remplies. De plus, la responsabilité est partagée entre l’employeur et l’employé (source : university.heavnn.io).

3. Ce que vous devez faire

Si vous êtes un employé étranger prévoyant de rester au Cambodge sur le long terme (idéalement plus de 182 jours en 12 mois), voici une liste simple :

  • Suivez attentivement votre présence physique : visas, tampons d’entrée/sortie, contrats de location peuvent servir de preuves

  • Coordonnez-vous avec votre employeur pour déposer une déclaration formelle de résidence fiscale auprès du GDT

  • Assurez-vous que la démarche est complétée par les deux parties afin de bénéficier du régime d’imposition progressif

Cette déclaration conjointe permet une classification correcte en tant que résident fiscal —

et donc, dans l’idéal, d’être imposé selon un barème plus avantageux, plutôt qu’au taux forfaitaire de 20 %.

Tableau récapitulatif

Statut Régime fiscal appliqué Déclaration requise ?
Étranger non-résident Taux forfaitaire de 20 % sur les revenus du Cambodge → Non, sauf demande spécifique
Étranger remplissant les critères Taux progressif (0–20 %) sur les revenus mondiaux → Oui, déclaration conjointe requise

item.title: Que se passe-t-il si mon permis de conduire expire au Cambodge ?
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Que se passe-t-il si mon permis de conduire expire au Cambodge ?

Si vous vivez au Cambodge, garder vos documents à jour — en particulier votre permis de conduire — est essentiel. Que vous soyez expatrié de longue durée ou résident local, connaître les règles de renouvellement de permis peut vous faire gagner du temps, de l’argent, et éviter bien des tracas.

Délai de grâce et pénalité quotidienne

Le Cambodge accorde un délai de grâce de 30 jours après la date d’expiration de votre permis de conduire.
Cependant, une fois ce délai dépassé, une pénalité quotidienne s’applique :

💸 500 riels par jour, à partir du 31e jour suivant l’expiration.

Exemple :
Si votre permis a expiré il y a 32 jours, vous paierez une amende pour 2 jours :
500 riels × 2 jours = 1 000 riels

Cela peut sembler négligeable au départ, mais plus vous attendez, plus le montant augmente.

Documents requis pour renouveler votre permis

Renouveler un permis de conduire expiré au Cambodge est relativement simple, à condition d’avoir les bons documents. Voici ce qu’il vous faudra généralement :

  • Votre ancien permis expiré

  • Une copie certifiée de votre carte d’identité cambodgienne (ou documents de résidence pour les étrangers)

  • Un certificat d’aptitude physique (généralement délivré par une clinique ou un hôpital local)

  • Des photos d’identité format passeport

Le renouvellement se fait dans des centres de service agréés, avec des frais variables selon le type de permis (moto, voiture, véhicule commercial).

🚨 Conduire avec un permis expiré ? Attendez-vous à une amende salée

Se faire contrôler avec un permis expiré n’est pas à prendre à la légère. Les amendes vont généralement de 30 $ à 60 $, selon la situation et son traitement.

En plus de l’amende, vous pourriez faire face à d’autres sanctions administratives, comme :

  • la mise en fourrière temporaire du véhicule

  • ou dans certains cas, l’obligation de repasser une partie de l’examen de conduite

Où renouveler son permis à Phnom Penh ?

Si vous êtes basé dans la capitale, vous pouvez renouveler votre permis à :

  • Le Département des Travaux Publics et des Transports (DPWT), rue 598

  • Les centres de service des centres commerciaux Aeon Mall (plus pratiques, mais souvent plus d’attente)

  • Ou encore via des agences intermédiaires, pratique si vous ne parlez pas couramment le khmer

👥 Conseil de AGCambodia

En tant qu’expatrié au Cambodge, garder vos documents à jour — notamment votre permis de conduire et votre assurance santé — est essentiel pour vivre en toute sérénité.

Et n’oubliez pas : si vous êtes assuré chez AGCambodia, nous proposons des services à valeur ajoutée et un accompagnement local pour les expatriés, que ce soit pour des démarches de permis ou des urgences médicales.

Besoin d’aide ?

L’équipe AGCambodia est là pour vous accompagner.
Pour des solutions d’assurance ou des conseils pratiques sur la vie au Royaume du Merveilleux, n’hésitez pas à passer à notre bureau ou à nous contacter en ligne.

📍 Adresse : 313 Sisowath Quay, Phnom Penh 12300
📧 Site web : www.agcambodia.com
📞 Téléphone / WhatsApp : 023 998 018

If you're living in Cambodia, keeping your documents in order\u2014especially your driver\u2019s license\u2014is essential. Whether you\u2019re a long-term expat or a local resident, knowing the ins and outs of license renewal can save you time, money, and hassle.<\/span><\/p>

So, what happens if your Cambodian driver\u2019s license expires? Let\u2019s break it down.<\/span><\/p>

Grace Period and Daily Penalty<\/b><\/span><\/h2>

Cambodia allows a 30-day grace period<\/b> after your driver's license has expired. However, once you pass that one-month window, a daily penalty kicks in. The fine is 500 riel per day<\/b>, starting from the 31st day of expiration.<\/span><\/p>

Example:<\/b><\/span><\/p>

If your license expired 32 days ago, you\u2019ll pay a fine for 2 days: 500 riel x 2 days = 1,000 riel<\/b><\/span><\/p>

While that may seem minimal, the longer you delay, the more it adds up.<\/span><\/p>

What You Need to Renew Your License<\/b><\/span><\/h2>

Renewing an expired Cambodian driver\u2019s license is fairly straightforward, as long as you have the right documents. Here\u2019s what you\u2019ll typically need:<\/span><\/p>

  • Your expired license<\/b><\/span><\/li>
  • A certified copy<\/b> of your Cambodian ID card (or residency documents if you're a foreigner)<\/span><\/li>
  • A physical fitness certificate<\/b> (usually issued by a local clinic or hospital)<\/span><\/li>
  • <\/b>Passport-sized photos<\/b><\/span><\/li><\/ul>

    You can complete the renewal at designated service centers, and the fees vary depending on the type of license (motorbike, car, or commercial vehicle).<\/span><\/p>

    <\/span> Driving with an Expired License? Expect a Hefty Fine<\/b><\/span><\/p>

    Getting caught driving with an expired license is not something to take lightly. Fines generally range between $30 to $60<\/b>, depending on the situation and how it's enforced.<\/span><\/p>

    Besides the fine, you may also face additional administrative hurdles, including temporary vehicle impoundment or the requirement to retake parts of your driving test in certain cases.<\/span><\/p>

    Where to Renew in Phnom Penh<\/b><\/span><\/h2>

    If you\u2019re based in the capital, license renewal can be done at:<\/span><\/p>

    • The Department of Public Works and Transport (DPWT)<\/b> on Street 598<\/span><\/li>
    • <\/b>Aeon Mall<\/b> service centers (for convenience, but expect longer wait times)<\/span><\/li>
    • Or consider using an agent service<\/b>, especially if you don\u2019t speak Khmer fluently<\/span><\/li><\/ul>

      <\/span> Tip from AGCambodia<\/b><\/span><\/p>

      As an expat in Cambodia, keeping your documents up to date\u2014especially your driver\u2019s license and health insurance\u2014is a big part of making your stay safe and stress-free.<\/span><\/p>

      And remember, if you're insured with AGCambodia<\/b>, we offer value-added services and local support for expats navigating everything from driver\u2019s licenses to medical emergencies.<\/span><\/p>

      Need Help?<\/b><\/span><\/h3>

      Our team at AGCambodia<\/b> is always here to assist. Whether you're looking for insurance solutions or helpful tips about living in the Kingdom of Wonder, drop by our office or get in touch online.<\/span><\/p>

      <\/span> Visit us:<\/b> 313 Sisowath Quay, Phnom Penh 12300
      <\/span><\/span> Website:<\/b> www.agcambodia.com<\/span><\/a>
      <\/span><\/span> Call or WhatsApp:<\/b><\/span><\/p>

      • 023 998 018<\/span><\/li><\/ul>","jedv_conditions":[{"_id":"cdf927a"}]},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":false}]

item.title: Cabinet Medical Francais - Dr Sebban
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Dr Michel Sebban – Médecin français à Phnom Penh

Le Docteur Michel Sebban, praticien français renommé, s’est installé au Cambodge en 2011. Avec son épouse, ils ont choisi de s’établir dans un pays qu’ils affectionnaient déjà, après avoir participé à plusieurs programmes internationaux visant à faciliter l’accès aux soins pour les populations défavorisées du Cambodge.

Son cabinet médical accueille les patients sur rendez-vous, du lundi au vendredi, pour des consultations en médecine générale.
Le Dr Sebban est également spécialiste dans trois domaines :

  • Gynécologie

  • Acupuncture

  • Homéopathie

Il est aujourd’hui le médecin de référence pour de nombreuses familles expatriées occidentales vivant au Cambodge.

Une équipe médicale française expérimentée

Le Dr Sebban est désormais entouré de plusieurs professionnels de santé français reconnus :

  • Dr Karin Ferret – Médecine tropicale & Urgences

  • Dr Isabelle de Gaudemar – ORL (oto-rhino-laryngologie)

  • Marie-Aimée Brichaux – Psychologue clinicienne

📍 Emplacement du Cabinet Médical Français

Le Cabinet Médical Français est situé à Phnom Penh,
Rue 118 (sens unique), depuis la rue 169, entre le boulevard Kampuchea Krom et le boulevard de la Confédération de Russie.

🏥 Recommandé par AG Cambodia

AG Cambodia recommande chaleureusement cette clinique aux expatriés en recherche de soins médicaux professionnels, en langue française, au cœur de Phnom Penh.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: AG Cambodia recommande le Cabinet Médical Français, fondé et dirigé par Monsieur et Madame Sebban depuis 2011.

item.title: Professional Indemnity
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
general insurance - private insurance

Professional Indemnity Insurance

When clients rely on your professional advice, expertise or services, an error can become a financial claim. Professional Indemnity Insurance protects businesses and professionals against claims alleging negligence, mistakes, omissions or a failure to deliver professional services as expected.

A claim does not always mean you did something wrong. A dissatisfied client may still allege that your advice, design, recommendation or work caused them a financial loss — and defending that allegation can involve significant legal costs even when the claim is ultimately unsuccessful.

Professional Indemnity is particularly relevant to consultants, architects, engineers, accountants, IT and technology companies, agencies and other businesses whose clients depend on their specialist knowledge or professional services. Cover can include eligible legal defence costs, settlements and compensation arising from insured claims, subject to the terms and limits of the policy.

item.title: Corporate Fleet insurance
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
general insurance - corporate insurance - vehicle

Professional Fleet Insurance

For companies operating cars, vans, trucks or other vehicles, motor insurance is both an operational necessity and a legal requirement. Third-party liability insurance is compulsory for company-registered vehicles in Cambodia, covering injury or property damage caused to others while your vehicles are in use.

Fleet policies can also extend to All Risks cover for damage or theft of your own vehicles, passenger liability and 24/7 claims assistance, including liaison with police and third parties following an accident. Through AG Cambodia, extended third-party liability limits can reach $100,000 per person and $500,000 per accident.

item.title: Business Property Insurance in Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
general insurance - corporate insurance

Property Insurance

Your premises are often one of the largest concentrations of value in your business. Business Property Insurance in Cambodia protects buildings, contents, equipment and other insured assets against physical loss or damage caused by risks such as fire, water damage, flood, explosion, windstorm, landslide and vehicle impact.

Often referred to locally as Fire Insurance, Property All Risks cover can be arranged for offices, shops, restaurants, hotels, warehouses, workshops, factories and other commercial premises. The value insured, use of the property and scope of cover all need to reflect how the business actually operates.

Get a Free quote

For risks valued below USD 50 million, Fire Insurance premiums follow an industry tariff, so the base price is standardised across insurers. The real differences lie in the cover provided, policy extensions, exclusions and how effectively the insurance has been structured around the risk.

Business Property Insurance is commonly combined with Public Liability and Business Interruption Insurance, helping protect not only the physical premises but also the income that may be lost if insured damage forces the business to stop or reduce operations.

Chat on Telegram

Get a quote

Your free property insurance quote

Ask us for a quotation to review the property, assets and business interruption exposure of your company and structure the appropriate cover.

Please enable JavaScript in your browser to complete this form.

item.title: Koh Russey Resort
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
special privilege offer for our policy holders

Koh Russey Resort

Pchum Ben Private Island Escape

3 Days / 2 Nights for Two — USD 1,150

Save $680 on the normal rates

10. 11. 12 October 2026

What you get as a Policy-Holder

✓ 2 nights in a
private pool villa

Two nights in a private pool villa, with a complimentary Beach Pool Villa upgrade, subject to availability.

 

✓ Daily breakfast
for two

Start each morning with a relaxed breakfast for two, included throughout your island stay.

 

✓ 60-minute massage
for two

Unwind together with a 60-minute massage for two at the resort spa.

✓ Snorkeling
experience

Discover the clear waters around Koh Russey with a complimentary snorkeling experience for two.

✓ Sun Downer
experience

End the day with a memorable sunset experience overlooking the island and sea.

✓ Romantic dinner
+ bottle of wine

Enjoy a romantic dinner for two, accompanied by a complimentary bottle of wine.

✓ Return speedboat transfers

Return scheduled speedboat transfers between Ream Pier and Koh Russey are included.

✓ 20% off additional
activities

Enjoy 20% off additional food & beverage, spa treatments and resort activities.

item.title: Calmette Hospital : the dean of hospitals
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded: Calmette Hospital – located on Monivong boulevard, near the French Embassy - remains the principal destination for road accidents. This hospital has greatly improved its service, noticeably with the introduction of its VIP wing and its "heart and cardio vascular" unit. This facility has also made important improvements in raising its operating standards to an International level. The arrival of a neuro surgeon, Mr François Xavier Roux, from France. Their other doctors have the experience and the skills to make a decision for surgery in life threatening cases that can’t wait the evacuation. The rates are also moderate... in comparison to other larger International hospitals. In case of life-threatening situations, AG Cambodia recommends Calmette Hospital.

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: In case of life-threatening situations, AG Cambodia recommends Calmette Hospital.

item.title: Sen Sok Hospital
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded: Sen Sok International University Hospital is the first International level hospital, run by the highly skilled and well experienced Physicians and Surgeons. All the facilities that you can expect from a hospital of the developed world; you can easily find them in the SSIUH. The prices are competitive with any other hospital in Cambodia and you will feel like a home environment in our hospital. The hospital houses 250 beds capacity, high-tech equipments, Laboratory, Pharmacy and makes use of the outstanding technology in the medical field and is well supported by a highly wholehearted, committed, competent and skilled medical team. Tel: 023 883 712 / 023 883 713 / Email: info@sensokiuh.com Address: Building 91-96, Street 1986, Phnom Penh Thmey, Khan Sen Sok, Phnom Penh, Cambodia. www.sensokiuh.com

item.title: Pharmacie de la gare
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
The "Pharmacie de la Gare" in Phnom Penh has been regarded as the most trustworthy drug vendor in the kingdom for several decades now. And rightfully so ! They had probably the most competent doctors and pharmacists, along with a wide selection of medicines and drugs, sometimes unavailable elsewhere in the country.
But, back in the 90's, they were competing with "want-to-be" pharmacists, opening shops everywhere without licenses nor competences. Today, the landscape has radically changed, and serious competitors have settled in the kingdom. U-care (http://www.ucarepharma.com/) for instance, has opened many branches in the country, and they distinguish themselves for being very professional, and patient-oriented. They carry only patented drugs that are regulated in the western world (EU & USA), you will find no copies or fakes, and expiring dates are meticulously checked. But they are other brands showing up here and there. This transition has also led smaller pharmacies to get on board and pay more attention to the products they sell.

item.title: Poe-ma closes its Cambodian branch

item.content:encoded: After more than 10 years in Cambodia, Poe-ma Assurances has chosen to stop its activities in the Kingdom. Poe-ma Cambodia passes all of its portfolio to AG Insurance Broker on the first of October this year. Nothing changes for our clients, their insurance contracts will be managed by the successful team of AG Insurance Broker. Founded in 2006 by Mr. David Treal, AG Insurance Broker is today the 1st brokerage firm in Cambodia. Like Poe-ma Cambodia, AG Insurance Broker is a French broker who provides specialized advice with local and international solutions, facilitating the management of your contracts and reimbursements and assisting you in the management of your claims. Poe-ma insurances Group thanks its customers and partners for their trust during these ten years.

item.title: Cabinet Medical Francais - Dr Sebban
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Michel Sebban Doctor Michel Sebban, a renowned French practitioner, settled in Cambodia in 2011. He and his wife chose a country that they loved for having participated in several International programs aimed at easing access to medical care for the poorer Cambodians. His office welcomes on appointment, every weekday  (Monday through Friday) for consultations for general medicine. However, Doctor Sebban has also 3 specialties : Gynecology, Acupuncture and Homeopathy. Dr. Sebban is currently doctor of many western expatriate families in Cambodia. But Doctor Sebban is not alone, today he is seconded by other remarkable French practitioners:
  • Dr. Karin Ferret (tropical health | Emergencies)
  • Dr Isabelle de Gaudemar (ORL)
  • Marie Aimée Brichaux (Psychologist)
The "Cabinet Médicale Français" is located on street 118 (one-way street) from street 169, between Kampuchea Krom Blvd &  Russian Confederation Blvd in Phnom Penh AG Cambodia recommends this clinic

item.title: Corona Virus (COVID-19) in Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Did you know?

Did you know ? Coronavirus is spreading through the world, hence not differently from most respiratory viral diseases. Do not panic as this is an infectious disease that has light and moderate symptoms for over 80% of people and it has a very low mortality rate (2%), however people with existing chronic respiratory conditions and weak health such as elderly or infants are most at risk. The number of infections is very limited to a very few cases in the Kingdom however it is good to know that you can get tested at l'Institut Pasteur or Khmer–Soviet Friendship Hospital. To avoid catching or spreading the disease , wash your hands with sanitizers and wear masks in public places. AG Cambodia is glad to confirm that its International Health Insurance plans cover Coronavirus treatment. Don’t hesitate to contact us today for more information or should you have any questions on your coverage.

item.title: What to do if you have Covid-19 in Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
If you stay in Phnom Penh:

  1. Contact to emergency number 115 to report your symptom.
  2. You can visit to Soviet hospital for the first consultation.
  3. After the consultation the doctor will send you to Pasteur Institute for the test according to his view of the symptom. The test is only available at Pasteur.
    **To the information that we have received from the Government, people will not be accepted to do Covid-19 test if they go directly to Pasteur without acknowledgement of the Government’s agency. The first monitoring is at Soviet Hospital only. **
  4.  If the result is positive you will be sent to Khmer-Soviet Hospital for treatment and quarantine.
 

If you stay in the province:

  1. Contact to emergency number 115 to report your symptom.
  2. You can to visit any public hospitals where is near you for the first consultation.
  3. The test will be only available at Public Hospitals. The blood sample will be sent to Pasteur Institute for further lab procedures.
  4. If the result is positive you will be sent to Khmer-Soviet Hospital for the treatment and quarantine. Each local health agency of the Ministry of Health Cambodia will arrange the evacuation to Phnom Penh.
 
**According to the recent declaration of the Cambodian Government, the first test will be free of charge for Cambodians and Expats. The whole treatment of Cambodian will be fully covered by the Government. There are some contribution that the patients need to participate such as foods, hygiene products (Sanitizer, Alcohol, Soap ) and etc.**

item.title: Why Is It Important To Have Home Insurance?
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
The house you live in is one of your most valuable possessions. You love it for all of its memories and comforts. The most important thing you can do is to ensure that it is completely secure.  In spite of the best security measures, there is always the possibility of theft, damage, and natural disasters, particularly fire, that we can never fully prevent. There are many ways in which these things can affect our lives and destroy our homes. 

"Last year, Cambodia experienced 670 fires that killed 19 people and injured 35. According to the Fire Prevention and Rescue Police Department, the number of fire incidents last year was a tremendous drop as compared with the 937 cases in 2020 " Khmer Times reported.

Protecting your home and family comforts is what home insurance is all about. Many of you will have saved for years in order to get the house of your dreams. In the case of a fire, you wouldn't be able to afford to make repairs without insurance, which is why it's so critical.  The insurer will pay for the repair or reinstatement of your lost property after a survey to assess the damage. With property insurance you guarantee the integrity of your real estate investment and ensure you are still in business in case of loss. 

To help you understand why this is true, we’ve listed the reasons you should have home insurance.

  1. The protection is not just for your home Coverage Inside and Outside, A home insurance policy protects not only the house from physical damage but also the items inside it.
  2. It replaces your loss

    Home insurance gives you financial security as well as the benefit of replacing your insured belongings. Depending on the home insurance policy you've chosen, you can now have your damaged property replaced instead of simply
    claiming an equivalent amount of money for your loss.
  3. It protects you from lawsuits

    Depending on the type of policy you choose, you can protect yourself and your family from property-related lawsuits. In the unfortunate event that you accidentally damage another property, such as a fire, your home insurance will cover you. Additionally, it will cover any medical expenses incurred by guests injured on your property.

     

  1. Peace of Mind

Getting your home insured provides you with the ultimate luxury of peace of mind. protecting your property is no longer your responsibility.

 

  1. It is affordable

A Home Insurance policy is one of the most affordable insurance policies. This small investment will protect your house against losses. There are several companies offering Home Insurance policies. Depending on the coverage offered, it is possible to choose the best Home Insurance policy for your home.

 

AG Cambodia, offering Home Insurance in Cambodia, provides exclusive package solutions to cover your condo or your house including Public Liability, Multi Risks content protection ( including theft), and Home helper accident cover.

Protect Your Home: Book an appointment online now

item.title: Buying residential apartment in Cambodia requires to have fire insurance for property?
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
In order to reduce the risk of a potential loss, insurance is a type of risk management. It is described as the fair assignment of loss risk from one organization to another in return for a premium. Insurance comes in a variety of forms, including life, health, disability, casualty, and property. and the insurer of the insured property is discussed in this article.

As the country's rate of home ownership grows, homeowners insurance and property insurance are becoming more and more popular among property owners in Cambodia.

Whether it’s your home or your business, you have probably invested a considerable amount of time, effort, and money in your property. Your property and investments will be protected against loss or damage if you have fire insurance. Property owners should have insurance in case unforeseen accident damage or destroy their property partially or completely. Compared to the high cost of replacing the property, an annual premium is far less financially burdensome.

Did you know that Cambodian residential apartments require fire insurance?

Some Cambodian residential apartments, but not all, demand the purchase of fire insurance for shared property. There is always a chance of fire damaging the apartment's belongings. Renters will have peace of mind knowing that their valuables are protected by fire insurance coverage. In the event of a fire, the insurance company will cover the costs. Such a situation is guarded against by fire insurance.

Fire insurance is the foundation of homeowners insurance in Cambodia.  It is a good place to start.  In the event that the insured wishes to cover additional risks or perils, endorsements to the policy are added and the premium is increased.  Any accidental loss or damage to the property, or contents if included, will be covered by the insurer for the perils covered.

item.title: Introduction to Insurance Needs in Cambodia: A Must-Have for Peace of Mind
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Whether you're an expatriate planning to move to Cambodia, a long-term resident, or a traveler embarking on a short visit, understanding and addressing your insurance needs is paramount. In a country that is as vibrant and dynamic as Cambodia, being prepared for the unexpected with reliable health and travel insurance isn't just a safety net—it's a necessity for peace of mind.

The Importance of Insurance in Cambodia

Cambodia, with its rich cultural heritage, stunning landscapes, and burgeoning economic opportunities, has become an attractive destination for people from all walks of life. However, like any country, it presents its own set of challenges and risks, from health concerns to travel disruptions. This is where the critical role of insurance comes into play. Health Insurance: A Safety Net for Medical Uncertainties Access to healthcare is one of the most pressing concerns for anyone in Cambodia. While the country is making strides in improving its healthcare facilities, the quality of care can vary significantly, especially outside major cities like Phnom Penh and Siem Reap. For more serious or specialized medical treatments, evacuation to a neighboring country might be necessary, which can be prohibitively expensive without adequate health insurance coverage. For expatriates and long-term residents, having a comprehensive health insurance plan ensures access to the best medical facilities without the burden of exorbitant costs. Short-term visitors, on the other hand, should not overlook the importance of travel health insurance to cover unexpected medical emergencies during their stay. Travel Insurance: Beyond Lost Luggage While lost luggage and flight cancellations are often the first things that come to mind with travel insurance, its scope extends far beyond these inconveniences. In Cambodia, where road conditions and traffic safety standards can be a concern, travel insurance becomes indispensable. It provides coverage for accidents and injuries, ensuring that unforeseen incidents do not turn into financial burdens. Moreover, for adventurers drawn to Cambodia's lush jungles and ancient ruins, travel insurance that covers activities like motorbiking, hiking, and exploring remote areas is crucial. These experiences, while enriching, come with their own set of risks, making appropriate insurance coverage a wise precaution.

Choosing the Right Insurance Partner

Navigating the complexities of insurance in a foreign country can be daunting. This is where partnering with a knowledgeable and reliable insurance broker like AG Cambodia becomes invaluable. With expertise in the local insurance landscape, AG Cambodia can guide you in selecting the right insurance products that meet your specific needs, ensuring that you are adequately protected. Whether it's helping expatriates find health insurance plans that cover international medical evacuation or advising travelers on the best travel insurance policies for their Cambodian adventure, AG Cambodia is committed to providing peace of mind to its clients.

Conclusion

Insurance in Cambodia is not just about mitigating risks—it's about ensuring that your time in the country is as worry-free and enjoyable as possible. By securing reliable health and travel insurance, you're investing in your well-being and peace of mind. With the right insurance coverage, you can focus on what truly matters: experiencing the beauty and opportunities that Cambodia has to offer.

item.title: Navigating the Complexities of Death in Cambodia: A Comprehensive Guide
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Death is a challenging and inevitable part of life, and dealing with it in a foreign country adds layers of complexity. Cambodia, with its rich cultural heritage and distinct legal framework, has specific protocols and practices for handling death. Here’s a detailed guide to help you navigate this difficult process.

1. Preparation Before Death

Register with the Consulate: If you’re an expatriate living in Cambodia, it’s prudent to register with your respective consulate or embassy. This registration can facilitate communication and assistance in case of emergencies. Inform Your Family: Clearly communicate your wishes regarding end-of-life arrangements with your family. This includes preferences for burial or cremation, repatriation of remains, and any specific rituals or ceremonies. Insurance: Securing comprehensive health and life insurance that covers repatriation and other associated costs is essential. Verify that your insurance policy is valid in Cambodia and understand the coverage details. Legal Arrangements: Consider consulting a local notary or legal expert to draft a will or other legal documents specifying your wishes. This step can prevent potential legal disputes and ensure your wishes are respected.

2. Immediate Steps After Death

Obtain a Death Certificate: The first and foremost step is to obtain a death certificate from a local hospital or the relevant Cambodian authorities. This document is crucial for all subsequent processes. Notify the Embassy or Consulate: Contact the deceased’s embassy or consulate. They can provide guidance and support, including assisting with the necessary paperwork and informing the next of kin. Inform the Insurance Company: Notify the deceased’s insurance company promptly. They will require a copy of the death certificate and other relevant documents to process any claims.

3. Handling the Remains

Repatriation or Local Burial: Decide whether the remains will be repatriated to the deceased’s home country or buried/cremated locally. Repatriation involves additional steps, including embalming and securing a coffin that meets international standards. The embassy can assist with these arrangements but note that the costs must be covered by the family. Local Burial or Cremation: If the choice is to handle the remains locally, engage with local funeral services. Cambodia has numerous funeral service providers familiar with both local customs and the needs of expatriates.

4. Administrative Procedures

Report to Local Authorities: Report the death to the local Cambodian authorities, such as the police, especially if the death occurred outside of a medical facility. This step is necessary for legal documentation and any potential investigations. Bank and Financial Accounts: Inform the relevant banks and financial institutions about the death. This notification helps in freezing accounts and preventing unauthorized transactions. Property and Assets: If the deceased owned property or other significant assets in Cambodia, initiate the legal process for the transfer or disposal of these assets. This process might require the services of a local attorney.

5. Cultural Sensitivities and Support

Respect Local Customs: Cambodia has its own set of cultural practices and traditions regarding death and funerals. Engaging with local customs respectfully can ease the process and provide a sense of closure. Seek Support: Don’t hesitate to seek emotional and logistical support from local expatriate communities, religious organizations, or grief counseling services.

Conclusion

Dealing with the death of a loved one is never easy, and doing so in a foreign country like Cambodia can be particularly daunting. However, with proper preparation, clear communication, and the right support, you can navigate this challenging time with greater ease. Ensure that you have all the necessary information and assistance by consulting with local authorities, your embassy, and legal experts. For further details and specific procedural information, refer to the comprehensive guide by Le Petit Journal here.

item.title: Do I Need Travel Insurance for Cambodia?
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Travel Health Insurance Requirements for Cambodia

As of 2022, Cambodia has relaxed its entry requirements, and travel health insurance is no longer mandatory for visitors. Previously, due to the Covid-19 pandemic, all travelers were required to have travel insurance. While it’s not required anymore, it’s still highly recommended to purchase a travel insurance policy before your trip. The Cambodian government suggests securing coverage of at least $50,000 for medical emergencies. Keep in mind that while travel insurance is suitable for short visits, such as tourism, those planning longer stays should consider obtaining comprehensive health insurance tailored for expats living in Cambodia.   More details here: visaguide.world

item.title: Exigences en matière d'assurance santé pour voyager au Cambodge
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Depuis 2022, le Cambodge a assoupli ses conditions d'entrée, et l'assurance santé de voyage n'est plus obligatoire pour les visiteurs. Auparavant, en raison de la pandémie de Covid-19, tous les voyageurs devaient souscrire une assurance voyage.
Bien que ce ne soit plus une obligation, il est toujours fortement recommandé de souscrire une assurance voyage avant votre départ. Le gouvernement cambodgien conseille de souscrire une couverture d'au moins 50 000 $ pour les urgences médicales.
Gardez à l'esprit que si l'assurance voyage est adaptée pour de courtes visites, telles que le tourisme, ceux qui prévoient de rester plus longtemps devraient envisager de souscrire une assurance santé complète destinée aux expatriés vivant au Cambodge.

item.title: L'assurance pour les véhicules sera bientôt obligatoire
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded: Le Régulateur des Assurances du Cambodge (IRC) a annoncé cette semaine que l'assurance obligatoire pour les véhicules sera "bientôt" mise en vigueur, ouvrant la voie à des compensations obligatoires en cas d'accident. Bou Chanphirou, Directeur Général de l'IRC, a déclaré lors de la célébration de la Journée de l'Assurance 2022, le 26 juillet, que les mécanismes ont déjà été préparés pour aller de l'avant avec l'application de cette mesure. « Nous les mettrons bientôt en œuvre pour tous les types de véhicules », a affirmé Chanphirou, sans donner de date précise. L'IRC a publié un communiqué le 27 juillet, précisant que l'assurance obligatoire des véhicules est une responsabilité financière et sécuritaire pour tous les conducteurs sur les routes publiques, et qu'elle est imposée dans presque tous les pays du monde. Les accidents de la route provoquent des difficultés financières pour les victimes qui doivent payer les frais médicaux et peuvent potentiellement perdre des revenus. Citant le Programme des Nations Unies pour le Développement (PNUD), l'IRC a indiqué que les pertes économiques liées aux accidents de la route en 2019 se sont élevées à 34 millions de dollars, en raison des dépenses médicales des blessés. L'IRC a ajouté que l'assurance des véhicules rend les propriétaires responsables de fournir une compensation aux victimes, soulignant que sans assurance, le fardeau repose sur les économies des personnes, les obligeant parfois à emprunter de l'argent, ce qui représente un sérieux poids pour les familles. « Par conséquent, acheter une assurance pour les véhicules ne devrait pas être perçu de manière négative ni comme une dépense importante, mais plutôt comme une planification financière personnelle pour se prémunir contre les risques d'accidents de la route », a déclaré l'IRC dans son communiqué. Saren, un chauffeur de taxi au Marché Central de Phnom Penh, a déclaré que l'assurance est bénéfique pour les personnes à revenu élevé, mais que ceux qui possèdent des voitures d'occasion n'ont pas les moyens d'acheter une assurance. « C'est difficile pour moi. Après tout, pour moi, quand nous avons un problème, c'est mauvais, mais si nous avons une assurance, c'est pratique », a expliqué Saren. Sinaro, qui travaille dans le marketing, a souligné qu'il est important pour le gouvernement d'étudier le revenu des gens avant de mettre en place une loi sur l'assurance. « En fait, je pense que c'est à la fois bon et mauvais, car c'est bien si l'État étudie les niveaux de revenus des gens, mais ce ne serait pas bon si leurs revenus dépassent cette obligation », a affirmé Sinaro. Actuellement, 94 compagnies d'assurance opèrent au Cambodge. Cela comprend 14 compagnies d'assurance vie, 18 compagnies d'assurance générale, sept petites compagnies d'assurance, une sous-compagnie d'assurance, 18 courtiers d'assurance, et 34 agences d'assurance. Deux sociétés d'évaluation des risques d'assurance exercent également des activités dans le secteur. Le marché de l'assurance au Cambodge était évalué à 300 millions de dollars en 2021, contribuant à hauteur de 1,1 % à l'économie cambodgienne, avec une densité d'assurance de 18,35 dollars par habitant.

item.title: Prendre sa retraite au Cambodge : Un guide pour les expatriés
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Voici une traduction complète en français de votre texte, adaptée en style informatif et fluide pour un guide à destination des futurs retraités au Cambodge :

Guide de la retraite au Cambodge : Visa, coût de la vie, santé, logement, et plus

Avec l'essor du tourisme au Cambodge – notamment grâce à l'augmentation des vols directs vers le Royaume – le pays devient une destination de plus en plus attractive, non seulement pour les voyageurs, mais aussi pour les retraités à la recherche d’une nouvelle vie à l’étranger. Réputé pour son cadre de vie agréable et abordable, le Cambodge attire de nombreux seniors venus profiter pleinement de leurs années dorées. Ce guide présente les informations essentielles à connaître pour envisager une retraite au Cambodge : visa, système bancaire, santé, coût de la vie, transport, et les meilleurs endroits où vivre.

🇰🇭 Visa Retraite

Le Cambodge propose une procédure simple pour les retraités grâce au visa ER, réservé aux ressortissants étrangers âgés de 55 ans ou plus. Ce visa peut être prolongé jusqu’à 12 mois, ce qui en fait une solution idéale pour une installation à long terme.

Étapes :

  1. Obtenez d’abord un visa de type E (E-class visa), en ligne ou via une ambassade/consulat du Cambodge.
  2. À votre arrivée dans le pays, transformez ce visa en visa ER via une agence spécialisée locale.

Documents requis :

  • Passeport valide (au moins 6 mois)
  • Une page vierge dans le passeport pour le visa
  • Photo d’identité (format passeport)
Contrairement à certaines informations circulant en ligne, il n’est pas obligatoire de justifier de revenus de retraite ou d’une pension, du moment que vous ne travaillez pas. L’administration considère que toute personne à la retraite dispose de ressources, qu'elles proviennent de revenus locatifs, d’épargne ou de l’aide de proches. 🔔 Mise à jour – 10 décembre 2024 : Selon Yvon Morvan (AEFC), il est désormais recommandé de fournir une preuve de revenus (ex. attestation de pension) traduite officiellement, mais cela reste à confirmer. 💰 Prix indicatif : Environ 300 $ pour un visa ER d’un an. Le visa peut être renouvelé indéfiniment, pour des périodes de 1, 3, 6 ou 12 mois.

💵 Monnaie & Banque

Le Cambodge utilise un système de double monnaie :
  • Le riel cambodgien (KHR)
  • Le dollar américain (USD)
Les billets USD sont largement utilisés, mais les petites coupures (1, 5, 10 $) deviennent rares, car la Banque nationale souhaite favoriser l’usage du riel pour les petites transactions. Depuis 2020, les paiements mobiles se sont généralisés : tous les établissements bancaires offrent des applications de paiement via QR code dynamique (KHQR). Il est donc courant de régler ses achats avec son téléphone, sans argent liquide.

Banques populaires auprès des expatriés :

  • ABA Bank
  • Canadia Bank
  • ACLEDA Bank
Les comptes peuvent être ouverts en riel ou en dollars. Il est aussi possible de recevoir votre pension sur un compte local via des services comme Western Union, MoneyGram, ou des transferts internationaux directs.

🏥 Santé

L'accès aux soins de qualité est une priorité pour les retraités. Le Cambodge a connu une amélioration significative de son système de santé ces dix dernières années, notamment dans le secteur privé.

Hôpitaux et cliniques à Phnom Penh :

  • Royal Phnom Penh Hospital
  • Hôpital Calmette
  • Intercare
  • Advance European Medicare Center
Les soins dentaires sont également abordables : 💳 À partir de 30 $ pour des soins de base Des pharmacies bien fournies, comme U-Care, proposent une large gamme de médicaments à des prix raisonnables. 👉 Le service Kampuchea Paramed propose des infirmiers à domicile, une option très appréciée des retraités. 💡 Il est fortement recommandé de souscrire une assurance santé internationale, couvrant les soins au Cambodge et à l’étranger.

🏠 Où vivre au Cambodge ?

Le Cambodge offre une diversité d’environnements selon vos préférences :

📍 Phnom Penh – La capitale dynamique

  • Parfaite pour ceux qui recherchent l’animation urbaine, avec centres commerciaux, infrastructures modernes, et vie culturelle riche.
  • Loyers :
    • ~200 $ pour un studio basique
    • ~700 $ ou plus pour un appartement moderne (quartiers BKK1, Tonle Bassac)
    • Jusqu’à 3 000 $ pour des résidences de luxe

📍 Siem Reap – La jungle culturelle

  • Ville à taille humaine, proche des temples d’Angkor Wat, avec une communauté expatriée conviviale.
  • Ambiance détendue, nature, et hébergements abordables.

📍 Kampot, Kep & Sihanoukville – Bord de mer et tranquillité

  • Kampot & Kep : atmosphère calme, charme provincial
  • Sihanoukville : ville côtière en plein essor, avec accès aux îles paradisiaques Koh Rong et Koh Rong Sanloem

🚖 Transport

Les transports sont nombreux, pratiques et économiques :
  • Tuk-tuk : parfaits pour les petits trajets urbains (1 à 3 $ selon la distance)
  • Moto & scooter : idéals pour plus d’autonomie
  • Bus : pour les trajets interurbains (environ 8 $)
  • Taxi privé : ~80 $ pour les destinations courantes
Applis recommandées pour réserver vos trajets : Grab, PassApp, etc.

💸 Coût de la vie au Cambodge

L’un des grands avantages de la retraite au Cambodge est son faible coût de la vie, comparé à l’Occident.

Estimation mensuelle moyenne à Phnom Penh :

Catégorie Coût estimé
Logement 200 $ à 700 $
Charges 50 $ à 100 $
Nourriture 150 $ à 1 500 $
Transport 50 $ à 100 $
💡 Conseils :
  • Vivre local permet d’économiser considérablement.
  • Les expatriés adeptes de produits occidentaux verront leur budget grimper.

✅ Conclusion

Choisir le Cambodge pour sa retraite, c’est profiter d’un style de vie agréable, d’un coût abordable, et d’un environnement accueillant. Grâce à la facilité d’obtention du visa, l’accès aux soins, une scène expatriée florissante et un climat ensoleillé, le Royaume du Merveilleux séduit de plus en plus de retraités du monde entier.
🆕 Mise à jour du 19 novembre 2025 D’après realestate.com.kh et le Khmer Times, de nouvelles conditions pour le visa retraite sont à l’étude :
  • Justificatif de pension ou de retraite
  • Certificat médical
  • Extrait de casier judiciaire
🔗 Source : Khmer Times – Guide to Retiring in Cambodia in 2026

item.title: Common Health Risks in Southeast Asia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Common Health Risks in Southeast Asia and Why Comprehensive Health Insurance is Crucial for Travelers and Expats

Southeast Asia is a captivating destination known for its vibrant cultures, beautiful landscapes, and rich history. However, this region also presents certain health risks that travelers and expats should be aware of. Understanding these risks and ensuring that you have comprehensive health insurance is critical for your safety and peace of mind during your time in Southeast Asia. In this guide, we’ll explore some of the most common health risks in Southeast Asia, discuss why health insurance is essential, and provide tips for staying healthy while enjoying your adventure in this part of the world.

1. Vector-Borne Diseases

Dengue Fever

Dengue fever (1), transmitted by the Aedes mosquito, is widespread across Southeast Asia, particularly during the rainy season. It can cause high fever, joint pain, and, in severe cases, hemorrhagic fever, which may require hospitalization. There is no specific treatment for dengue, making prevention and early detection critical. Rehydratation and rest are the most effective cure, in serious cases, this should be done under medical supervision, e.i. hospitalisation.

Malaria

While not as prevalent as dengue, malaria is still a risk in rural and forested areas of Southeast Asia, especially in countries like Cambodia, Laos, and Myanmar. Symptoms include fever, chills, and flu-like illness, and without prompt treatment, malaria can be fatal.

Chikungunya and Japanese Encephalitis

Other mosquito-borne diseases like chikungunya and Japanese encephalitis are also found in parts of Southeast Asia. Both illnesses have the potential for serious complications, especially Japanese encephalitis, which can cause brain swelling and long-term neurological issues. Prevention Tips:
  • Use mosquito repellent containing DEET or picaridin.
  • Wear long sleeves and pants, particularly during early morning and evening.
  • Stay in accommodations with air conditioning or properly screened windows.

2. Food and Waterborne Illnesses

Traveler’s Diarrhea

Food and waterborne diseases are among the most common ailments that affect travelers and expats in Southeast Asia. Traveler’s diarrhea, caused by consuming contaminated food or water, can range from mild to severe, requiring medical attention if dehydration occurs.

Hepatitis A and E

Hepatitis A and E are viral infections transmitted through contaminated food and water, prevalent in many parts of Southeast Asia. Hepatitis A can cause liver inflammation, fatigue, and jaundice, while Hepatitis E is especially dangerous for pregnant women.

Typhoid Fever

Typhoid fever, another bacterial infection spread through contaminated food and water, can lead to high fever, abdominal pain, and potentially life-threatening complications if left untreated. Prevention Tips:
  • Drink only bottled or purified water.
  • Avoid street food from unsanitary vendors.
  • Practice good hand hygiene, especially before eating.

3. Air Pollution and Respiratory Issues

Haze and Poor Air Quality

Several Southeast Asian countries experience seasonal air pollution known as “haze,” often caused by agricultural fires in the region. Cities like Bangkok, Jakarta, and Hanoi can experience high levels of air pollution, which may exacerbate respiratory conditions such as asthma or cause short-term health effects like coughing, shortness of breath, and sore throat. Prevention Tips:
  • Monitor air quality using apps and websites.
  • Wear an N95 mask on days when pollution levels are high.
  • Avoid outdoor activities during heavy pollution periods.
[caption id="attachment_4866" align="alignnone" width="1200"] health issues in south east asia[/caption]

4. Tropical Skin Infections and Heat-Related Illnesses

Fungal and Bacterial Skin Infections

The hot and humid climate in Southeast Asia makes it easy for fungal and bacterial skin infections to develop, particularly in cuts, scrapes, or areas prone to sweat. Infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, and impetigo can cause discomfort and may require medical treatment.

Heat Stroke and Dehydration

With high temperatures and intense humidity, travelers and expats are at risk of heat stroke and dehydration, particularly during outdoor activities or long travel days. Heat stroke can be life-threatening if not addressed quickly. Prevention Tips:
  • Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water.
  • Wear loose-fitting, breathable clothing.
  • Take breaks in shaded or air-conditioned areas during the hottest parts of the day.

5. Rabies

Rabies is a risk in many parts of Southeast Asia, particularly in areas with stray animals, such as dogs, monkeys, and bats. A bite or scratch from an infected animal can transmit the virus, and if left untreated, rabies is almost always fatal. Prevention Tips:
  • Avoid direct contact with animals, especially strays.
  • Get a rabies vaccination if you plan to travel to rural or high-risk areas.
  • Seek immediate medical attention if bitten or scratched.

6. Road Accidents and Trauma

Traffic Risks

Southeast Asia is known for chaotic traffic conditions, especially in major cities like Bangkok, Ho Chi Minh City, and Manila. Road accidents are a leading cause of injury for travelers and expats in the region, and access to emergency care may vary, particularly in remote areas. Prevention Tips:
  • Wear helmets when riding motorcycles or scooters.
  • Avoid traveling by road at night in rural areas.
  • Use reputable transportation services when available.

The Importance of Comprehensive Health Insurance

Given the range of health risks in Southeast Asia, having comprehensive health insurance is not only advisable but necessary for anyone spending time in the region. Here’s why:

1. Access to Quality Healthcare

Some Southeast Asian countries have excellent private hospitals, especially in urban centers like Bangkok and Singapore. However, these facilities can be expensive, especially for major treatments or emergency services. Comprehensive health insurance ensures that you can access high-quality care without worrying about prohibitive costs.

2. Coverage for Emergencies

Accidents and sudden illnesses can happen when you least expect them. Comprehensive health insurance covers emergencies like severe dengue fever, road accidents, or even air evacuations if necessary. Without coverage, these situations can result in exorbitant medical bills.

3. Vaccinations and Preventive Care

A good health insurance policy will cover vaccinations for diseases such as hepatitis, typhoid, and rabies, which are essential for protecting your health in Southeast Asia. Preventive care, including regular check-ups, can help detect any issues before they become serious.

4. Coverage for Evacuation and Repatriation

In the case of severe illness or injury, evacuation to a neighboring country or even your home country may be required. Medical evacuations can be costly, but comprehensive health insurance will cover these expenses, ensuring you receive the best care available.

Conclusion

While Southeast Asia is an incredible place to live and explore, it’s essential to be aware of the potential health risks and take steps to protect yourself. From mosquito-borne diseases to road accidents, having comprehensive health insurance gives you the security and peace of mind to enjoy your time in this vibrant region fully. When planning your trip or long-term stay in Southeast Asia, make sure to research and invest in a health insurance policy that covers both routine and emergency care. After all, nothing is more valuable than your health and well-being.

item.title: The Crucial Role of the Institut Pasteur du Cambodge in Strengthening Cambodia’s Agri-Food Sector
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded: Cambodia’s agriculture sector is key to its economic growth, but achieving international standards for food safety remains a challenge. Thanks to the collaboration between Australia and the Institut Pasteur du Cambodge (IPC), supported by the CAPRED program, local businesses now have access to ISO 17025-accredited testing services. These labs will test for pesticide, antibiotic, and heavy metal residues, enhancing product safety and quality. This initiative is transformative, reducing reliance on costly foreign services and improving the competitiveness of Cambodian products in both local and international markets. By establishing cutting-edge laboratories, IPC is not only bolstering food safety but also creating sustainable development opportunities through increased market access and export readiness. Moreover, this collaboration significantly aids local businesses, especially women-owned enterprises, by equipping them with the tools to meet stringent international standards. IPC’s role in this development is pivotal, ensuring the Cambodian agri-food sector’s long-term resilience and competitiveness. More information: https://www.khmertimeskh.com/501575518/australia-partners-with-institut-pasteur-du-cambodge-to-promote-food-safety-and-exports/ #FoodSafety #Sustainability #AgriBusiness #Cambodia #InstitutPasteurDuCambodge #AustraliaPartnership #CAPRED

item.title: Why Kampuchea Paramed is Revolutionizing Healthcare in Cambodia
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
Introduction In Cambodia’s rapidly evolving healthcare landscape, reliable home medical care is becoming essential, especially for expatriates and locals seeking high-quality medical services. Kampuchea Paramed has emerged as a trusted provider, offering professional nursing care and medical support services in Phnom Penh. In this post, we explore what makes Kampuchea Paramed a game-changer in Cambodia's healthcare system.

Who is Kampuchea Paramed?

Founded in 2020 by three experienced French-certified nurses, Kampuchea Paramed specializes in home-based medical care and healthcare services tailored to individuals, families, and businesses. Their mission is to provide world-class healthcare while improving local health systems and nursing standards in Cambodia.

Services You Can Trust

1. Home and Office Nursing Care Kampuchea Paramed’s team delivers personalized medical care, including:
  • Post-surgical care
  • Wound dressings and injections
  • Elderly and disabled care
  • Chronic illness management
These services help patients recover comfortably at home, reducing the need for hospital stays. 2. Hospitalization at Home For patients needing continuous medical attention, Kampuchea Paramed provides professional care at home, including:
  • Medical monitoring
  • Equipment installation (hospital beds, oxygen therapy)
  • Environmental adaptations for patient comfort
3. Medical Support for Companies and Events Businesses can ensure a safer work environment with Kampuchea Paramed’s corporate health services. They offer on-site medical assistance, health consultations, and even event medical coverage for emergencies. 4. Medical Escort & Repatriation Medical emergencies requiring evacuation can be stressful. Kampuchea Paramed organizes professional medical repatriation and escorts, ensuring patients receive specialized care while traveling to their home country or a suitable healthcare facility. 5. Health Training & Education They also provide certified first aid and health training courses for individuals and businesses, ensuring health preparedness in emergencies.

Why Choose Kampuchea Paramed?

  1. Experienced Team: With a background in European healthcare standards, the team brings extensive international experience to Cambodia.
  2. Personalized Care Plans: Each patient receives customized care based on their medical history and specific needs.
  3. 24/7 Availability: They are always ready to respond to emergencies, making healthcare accessible and dependable.
  4. Multilingual Support: English, French, and Khmer-speaking staff provide a seamless experience for locals and expatriates alike.

Conclusion

Kampuchea Paramed is setting new standards for home healthcare services in Cambodia. Whether you are an expatriate living in Phnom Penh or a local resident needing professional nursing care, their compassionate and highly skilled team ensures that quality healthcare is never out of reach. Need Medical Assistance in Cambodia? Visit Kampuchea Paramed or contact them today for personalized healthcare services.

item.title: Retiring in Cambodia: A Guide for Expats
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
With Cambodia's tourism on the rise, thanks to an increase in direct flights to the Kingdom, the country is becoming an increasingly attractive destination not only for travelers but also for retirees looking for a new home abroad. Cambodia has earned a reputation as a pleasant and affordable place for seniors to enjoy their golden years. This guide will cover the essentials for aspiring expats considering retirement in Cambodia, including visa options, currency and banking, healthcare, cost of living, transportation, and the best places to live.

Retirement Visa

Cambodia offers a straightforward visa process for retirees through its ER visa program, designed for foreign citizens aged only 55 and over. This visa can be extended for up to 12 months, making it an appealing option for those looking to settle long-term in the Kingdom. To obtain a retirement visa, you first need to apply for a regular E-class visa, which can be done through a Cambodian Embassy or Consulate in your home country or online. Once you arrive in Cambodia, you will need to convert this into an ER retirement visa through a local visa agency, which will assist with the application process. The following documents are required for the ER visa application:
  • A passport with at least six months of validity
  • A blank passport page for the visa
  • A passport-sized photo
Unlike information posted on other websites, there is no need for prove of any pension or retirement scheme. Since it is absolutely forbidden for you to get a paid job in the Kingdom, you will have some kind of financial resources. So it does not matter if you collect rent from your hometown or if your children are financing your stay here, the immigration department will not ask. As of the most recent updates, the cost for the ER visa is around $300 for one year. The visa can be renewed or extended for periods of 1, 3, 6, or 12 months, depending on your plans, and as of today, the visa can be extended an infinite number of times. Update December 10, 2024: According to the AEFC's representative Yvon Morvan, the government is currently requiring ER visa's applicants for proof of income, namely the documentation of a pension. This document should be officially translated. This information remains to be confirmed.

Currency & Banking

Cambodia operates with a dual currency system, using both the Cambodian riel (KHR) and the US dollar (USD). While US notes are widely accepted for most transactions, the National Bank of Cambodia is pushing to de-dollarise smaller purchase, as such the small dollar notes (1, 5 and 10's) are slowly, but surely being scarce. List of all the banks in 2024. Also, note that Cambodia is very modern in terms of banking and payment facilities; since 2020, everyone pays with their mobile phone. Every bank in the country offer the payment app, using the KHor a dynamic QRcode payment system. So, most of the time you won't have much cash to carry, all you need is your smart phone. When it comes to banking, major institutions like ABA Bank, Canadia Bank, and ACLEDA Bank are popular choices among expats. You can open accounts in either riel or dollars, depending on your preference. Retirees can also transfer their pension funds to any local bank, which can be easily done through various international money transfer services available in Phnom Penh, including Western Union and MoneyGram.

Healthcare

Access to quality healthcare is a crucial consideration for retirees. Cambodia's healthcare system has improved significantly over the past decade, with a growing number of private clinics and continuous development in the public sector. Leading hospitals in Phnom Penh include the Royal Phnom Penh Hospital, Calmette Hospital, and specialized clinics like Intercare and Advance European Medicare Center. Dental care is also affordable and of good quality, with prices for basic services starting from $30. Pharmacies are plentiful and offer a wide range of affordable medications, notably U-care. Another player in the scenery that might interest people looking to retire in Cambodia, is Kampuchea Paramed, which offers mobile nursing services. This means you can have the visit of nurses directly to your home. Read More Many retirees opt to purchase health insurance that covers medical treatment both in Cambodia and abroad. It's wise to research healthcare options thoroughly and consider including medical expenses in your retirement budget. https://youtu.be/XItB-et9QL0?si=oCnnj15XeiJcaZg0

Where to Live

Cambodia offers diverse living environments to suit different preferences. For those who enjoy city life, Phnom Penh is the bustling capital where most economic activities take place. The city is rapidly developing, with new shopping malls, high-rise buildings, and modern amenities. Renting in Phnom Penh can range from $200 for a basic studio to $700 or more for a modern apartment in prime areas like BKK1 or Tonle Bassac. Apartments under $300 For a more relaxed lifestyle, Siem Reap is a favored destination, especially for its proximity to the world-renowned Angkor Wat temple complex. Known for its expat community and vibrant entertainment scene, Siem Reap offers a jungle-like environment with quality accommodations available at reasonable prices. Other popular retirement spots include Sihanoukville, Kampot, and Kep. Sihanoukville has seen substantial development, offering beachside living and easy access to the islands of Koh Rong and Koh Rong Sanloem. Kampot and Kep are known for their slow-paced lifestyle, attracting retirees who prefer a peaceful countryside setting.

Transportation

Transportation in Cambodia is affordable and varied, with options including tuk-tuks, motorbikes, buses, and even trains. Tuk-tuks are commonly used for short city trips, while motorbikes are popular for longer journeys. Buses are available for intercity travel, though it's important to be mindful of road safety, which may not meet Western standards.

Cost of Living

One of the key advantages of retiring in Cambodia is its low cost of living. Housing, utilities, transportation, food, and entertainment are generally much more affordable than in many Western countries. Living costs vary depending on your location and lifestyle, with Phnom Penh being slightly more expensive than other areas. Here’s a rough estimate of average monthly expenses in Phnom Penh:
  • Housing: $200-$700. You can live like a Cambodian in the center of the city, in an older building, or choose one of those modern condominium. Note that the large luxurious condo could charge up to $3,000 per month the high end of their catalog
  • Utilities: $50-$100. This will depend on your consumption of Air Conditioning. Most expat will use it in evening before bedtime. But should you want ot need AC all day long, best to move in a condo.
  • Food: $150-$1,500. If you can eat local food everyday, then your budget will be around $150, but should you want to keep your western eating habits, imported products will jack up your budget quite rapidly. Phnom Penh enjoys a very wide spectrum in terms of dining out: from the local family restaurant near your house to the luxurious sky high French restaurant. As you would expect, the price difference is considerable.
  • Transportation: $50-$100. Yes, quick transportation within the city area is quite affordable. Each ride will start at about a dollar up to 2 or 3 dollars, depending on the distance. You can negotiate yourself with the driver, or simply use any taxi app to order and pay for your ride. Traveling within Cambodia, a bus ticket will be about $8 and a private taxi around 80$ for the most common destinations

Conclusion

Retiring in Cambodia offers a unique opportunity to enjoy a high quality of life at an affordable cost. With the ease of obtaining a retirement visa, access to healthcare, a variety of living environments, and a low cost of living, it’s no wonder that Cambodia is becoming a popular choice for retirees from around the world.   November 19, 2025 Updates from a realestate.com.kh and Khmertimes https://www.khmertimeskh.com/501792115/guide-to-retiring-in-cambodia-in-2026/ They added some prerequisites: - Proof of retirement or pension scheme - Health certificate - Criminal background check

item.title: What Happens If my Driver’s License Expires in Cambodia?
item.dc:creator: agadmin
item.content:encoded:
If you're living in Cambodia, keeping your documents in order—especially your driver’s license—is essential. Whether you’re a long-term expat or a local resident, knowing the ins and outs of license renewal can save you time, money, and hassle. So, what happens if your Cambodian driver’s license expires? Let’s break it down.

Grace Period and Daily Penalty

Cambodia allows a 30-day grace period after your driver's license has expired. However, once you pass that one-month window, a daily penalty kicks in. The fine is 500 riel per day, starting from the 31st day of expiration. Example: If your license expired 32 days ago, you’ll pay a fine for 2 days: 500 riel x 2 days = 1,000 riel While that may seem minimal, the longer you delay, the more it adds up.

What You Need to Renew Your License

Renewing an expired Cambodian driver’s license is fairly straightforward, as long as you have the right documents. Here’s what you’ll typically need:
  • Your expired license
  • A certified copy of your Cambodian ID card (or residency documents if you're a foreigner)
  • A physical fitness certificate (usually issued by a local clinic or hospital)
  • Passport-sized photos
You can complete the renewal at designated service centers, and the fees vary depending on the type of license (motorbike, car, or commercial vehicle). Driving with an Expired License? Expect a Hefty Fine Getting caught driving with an expired license is not something to take lightly. Fines generally range between $30 to $60, depending on the situation and how it's enforced. Besides the fine, you may also face additional administrative hurdles, including temporary vehicle impoundment or the requirement to retake parts of your driving test in certain cases.

Where to Renew in Phnom Penh

If you’re based in the capital, license renewal can be done at:
  • The Department of Public Works and Transport (DPWT) on Street 598
  • Aeon Mall service centers (for convenience, but expect longer wait times)
  • Or consider using an agent service, especially if you don’t speak Khmer fluently
Tip from AGCambodia As an expat in Cambodia, keeping your documents up to date—especially your driver’s license and health insurance—is a big part of making your stay safe and stress-free. And remember, if you're insured with AGCambodia, we offer value-added services and local support for expats navigating everything from driver’s licenses to medical emergencies.

Need Help?

Our team at AGCambodia is always here to assist. Whether you're looking for insurance solutions or helpful tips about living in the Kingdom of Wonder, drop by our office or get in touch online. Visit us: 313 Sisowath Quay, Phnom Penh 12300 Website: www.agcambodia.com Call or WhatsApp:
  • 023 998 018
